I'm noticing the timing alignment here—the user's second message came through at 17:02:39, and at that exact same timestamp there are two sequential events: a worker selection change followed by the system waiting for user input. The artifact sequence numbers suggest these events are closely tied together.

Looking at the data, the messages table only contains the two user inputs, no assistant responses—so the agent's output must be stored in artifact_streams instead. 1	/**
2	 * Shared bytes-level append-only artifact storage.
3	 *
4	 * Modelled on the worker output-store JSONL+gzip+lock pattern. Every
5	 * stream is identified by (runId, kind, ownerId) and lives at a
6	 * stream-relative path inside the run's artifact root. The bytes layer
7	 * knows about:
8	 *
9	 *   - JSONL append with a guard for crash-truncated tail lines
10	 *   - Per-stream serialization via an in-process write chain + an
11	 *     OS-visible lock directory (covers dev process restarts and
12	 *     parallel module instances)
13	 *   - Tail-scan reading with a parameterized line predicate so callers
14	 *     can terminate early on a cursor boundary
15	 *   - Gzip compaction of inactive streams to `<stream>.jsonl.gz`
16	 *   - Expanding `.jsonl.gz` back to plaintext on a fresh append
17	 *   - Read-side `(size, mtimeMs)` cache invariants so unchanged files
18	 *     return without I/O on repeat polls
19	 *
20	 * Domain semantics — entry dedup, history truncation, legacy DB
21	 * fallbacks, archive zips, schema-level normalization — live in the
22	 * per-domain adapter (e.g. worker output-store). This module is
23	 * deliberately ignorant of them.
24	 */

53	const FILE_LOCK_MIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 25;
54	const FILE_LOCK_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS = 250;

57	// --- Public types ----------------------------------------------------
58	
59	export interface ArtifactStreamLocation {

61	  id: ArtifactStreamId;
62	  /** Resolved artifact root (project-local or legacy global fallback). */
63	  root: ArtifactRoot;
64	  /**

66	   * `artifact_streams.relative_path`. Forward-slash separated for

68	   */
69	  relativeStreamPath: string;
70	  /** Absolute path of the plaintext `.jsonl` file. */
71	  filePath: string;
72	  /** Absolute path of the gzipped variant `<stream>.jsonl.gz`. */
73	  compressedFilePath: string;
74	  /** Absolute path of the lock directory. */
75	  lockPath: string;
76	}
77	
78	export interface AppendOptions {
79	  /** ID used to make the append idempotent. Re-appending the same id is a no-op. */
80	  recordId?: string | null;
81	}
82	
83	export interface ReadEntriesSinceOptions {
84	  /** Maximum bytes to walk back from the file end. Default 1 MiB. */
85	  maxBytes?: number;
86	  /** Chunk size when reading the tail. Default 64 KiB. */
87	  chunkSize?: number;
88	}
89	
90	// --- Path / identity helpers ----------------------------------------
91	
92	export function streamRelativePath(id: ArtifactStreamId): string {
93	  switch (id.kind) {
94	    case "worker_entries": {
95	      const ownerId = id.ownerId?.trim();
96	      if (!ownerId) {
97	        throw new Error(`Worker artifact stream requires an ownerId (workerId).`);
98	      }
99	      return `workers/${ownerId}.jsonl`;
100	    }
101	    case "execution_events":
102	      return "execution-events.jsonl";
103	    case "supervisor_interventions":
104	      return "supervisor-interventions.jsonl";
105	    case "planning_review_findings":
106	      return "planning-review-findings.jsonl";
107	    default: {
108	      // Exhaustiveness guard.
109	      const _exhaustive: never = id.kind;
110	      throw new Error(`Unknown artifact stream kind: ${_exhaustive}`);
111	    }
112	  }
113	}
114	
115	export async function resolveArtifactStreamLocation(
116	  args: {
117	    runId: string;
118	    kind: ArtifactStreamId["kind"];
119	    ownerId: string | null;
120	    projectPath: string | null | undefined;
121	  },
122	  mode: "read" | "write",
123	): Promise<ArtifactStreamLocation> {
124	  const id: ArtifactStreamId = {
125	    runId: args.runId,
126	    kind: args.kind,
127	    ownerId: args.ownerId,
128	  };
129	  const root = await resolveArtifactRoot({ runId: args.runId, projectPath: args.projectPath }, mode);
130	  const relativeStreamPath = streamRelativePath(id);
131	  const filePath = resolveStreamPathWithin(root, relativeStreamPath);
132	  const compressedFilePath = `${filePath}.gz`;
133	  const lockPath = `${filePath}.lock`;
134	  return { id, root, relativeStreamPath, filePath, compressedFilePath, lockPath };
135	}
136	
137	// --- In-process write chain -----------------------------------------
138	
139	const writeChainsByKey = new Map<string, Promise<void>>();
140	
141	function chainKey(id: ArtifactStreamId) {
142	  const owner = normalizeArtifactOwnerId(id.ownerId);
143	  return `${id.kind}::${id.runId}::${owner === ARTIFACT_STREAM_OWNER_NONE ? "_" : owner}`;
144	}
145	
146	export function runOnArtifactChain<T>(id: ArtifactStreamId, task: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
147	  const key = chainKey(id);
148	  const previous = writeChainsByKey.get(key) ?? Promise.resolve();
149	  const next = previous.then(() => task());
150	  const tracked = next.then(() => undefined, () => undefined);
151	  writeChainsByKey.set(key, tracked);
152	  return next.finally(() => {
153	    if (writeChainsByKey.get(key) === tracked) {
154	      writeChainsByKey.delete(key);
155	    }
156	  });
157	}
158	
159	// --- File lock (mkdir-based, OS-visible) ----------------------------
160	
161	function sleep(ms: number) {
162	  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
163	}
164	
165	function fileLockDelay(attempt: number) {
166	  const delay = FILE_LOCK_MIN_TIMEOUT_MS * (FILE_LOCK_FACTOR ** attempt);
167	  return Math.min(Math.round(delay), FILE_LOCK_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS);
168	}
169	
170	function isRecoverableLockRaceError(error: unknown) {
171	  const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
172	  return code === "ENOENT" || code === "ENOTDIR" || code === "EINVAL";
173	}
174	
175	async function isFileLockStale(lockPath: string) {
176	  try {
177	    const stat = await fs.stat(lockPath);
178	    try {
179	      await fs.access(path.join(lockPath, "owner.json"));
180	    } catch (error) {
181	      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
182	        return true;
183	      }
184	      throw error;
185	    }
186	    return stat.mtimeMs < Date.now() - FILE_LOCK_STALE_MS;
187	  } catch (error) {
188	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
189	      return true;
190	    }
191	    throw error;
192	  }
193	}
194	
195	async function acquireArtifactFileLock(lockPath: string): Promise<() => Promise<void>> {
196	  const ownerPath = path.join(lockPath, "owner.json");
197	  const ownerToken = randomUUID();
198	  const owner = JSON.stringify({
199	    token: [REDACTED]
200	    pid: process.pid,
201	    createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
202	  });
203	
204	  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= FILE_LOCK_RETRIES; attempt += 1) {
205	    try {
206	      await fs.mkdir(lockPath);
207	      try {
208	        await fs.writeFile(ownerPath, owner, "utf8");
209	      } catch (error) {
210	        await fs.rm(lockPath, { recursive: true, force: true });
211	        if (isRecoverableLockRaceError(error)) {
212	          continue;
213	        }
214	        throw error;
215	      }
216	
217	      let released = false;
218	      const refresh = async () => {
219	        if (released) return;
220	        const now = new Date();
221	        await fs.utimes(lockPath, now, now);
222	        await fs.utimes(ownerPath, now, now);
223	      };
224	      const interval = setInterval(() => {
225	        void refresh().catch(() => {});
226	      }, FILE_LOCK_UPDATE_MS);
227	      interval.unref?.();
228	
229	      return async () => {
230	        if (released) return;
231	        released = true;
232	        clearInterval(interval);
233	        try {
234	          const currentOwner = await fs.readFile(ownerPath, "utf8");
235	          if (currentOwner !== owner) return;
236	        } catch (error) {
237	          if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return;
238	          throw error;
239	        }
240	        await fs.rm(lockPath, { recursive: true, force: true });
241	      };
242	    } catch (error) {
243	      const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
244	      if (code !== "EEXIST") throw error;
245	
246	      if (await isFileLockStale(lockPath)) {
247	        await fs.rm(lockPath, { recursive: true, force: true });
248	        continue;
249	      }
250	      if (attempt === FILE_LOCK_RETRIES) {
251	        throw Object.assign(new Error(`Timed out waiting for artifact lock: ${lockPath}`), {
252	          code: "ELOCKED",
253	        });
254	      }
255	      await sleep(fileLockDelay(attempt));
256	    }
257	  }
258	
259	  throw Object.assign(new Error(`Timed out waiting for artifact lock: ${lockPath}`), {
260	    code: "ELOCKED",
261	  });
262	}
263	
264	export async function withArtifactFileLock<T>(location: ArtifactStreamLocation, task: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
265	  await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(location.filePath), { recursive: true });
266	  // Atomic touch so a fresh stream has something to lock against.
267	  await fs.writeFile(location.filePath, "", { flag: "a" });
268	  const release = await acquireArtifactFileLock(location.lockPath);
269	  try {
270	    return await task();
271	  } finally {
272	    await release();
273	  }
274	}
275	
276	// --- JSONL helpers --------------------------------------------------
277	
278	export function parseJsonlLines<T>(body: string): T[] {
279	  const out: T[] = [];
280	  for (const line of body.split("\n")) {
281	    const trimmed = line.trim();
282	    if (!trimmed) continue;
283	    try {
284	      const parsed = JSON.parse(trimmed);
285	      if (parsed && typeof parsed === "object") {
286	        out.push(parsed as T);
287	      }
288	    } catch {
289	      // Skip malformed (e.g. truncated last line after crash).
290	    }
291	  }
292	  return out;
293	}
294	
295	export async function needsLeadingNewline(target: string): Promise<boolean> {
296	  try {
297	    const stat = await fs.stat(target);
298	    if (stat.size === 0) return false;
299	    const handle = await fs.open(target, "r");
300	    try {
301	      const buf = Buffer.alloc(1);
302	      await handle.read(buf, 0, 1, stat.size - 1);
303	      return buf[0] !== 0x0a;
304	    } finally {
305	      await handle.close();
306	    }
307	  } catch (error) {
308	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return false;
309	    throw error;
310	  }
311	}
312	
313	// --- File-state cache for read-side short-circuit ------------------
314	
315	interface FileStateSnapshot {
316	  size: number;
317	  mtimeMs: number;
318	}
319	
320	export async function readFileState(filePath: string): Promise<FileStateSnapshot | null> {
321	  try {
322	    const s = await fs.stat(filePath);
323	    return { size: s.size, mtimeMs: s.mtimeMs };
324	  } catch (error) {
325	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return null;
326	    throw error;
327	  }
328	}
329	
330	// --- Append --------------------------------------------------------
331	
332	/**
333	 * Append one JSON-encoded record line to the stream. The caller is
334	 * responsible for assigning the record's `seq` and serializing the
335	 * JSON (so domain-specific shapes — e.g. the worker entry record vs
336	 * the run-level envelope — stay in adapters).
337	 *
338	 * When `seq` is provided, the bytes layer also maintains a sparse
339	 * companion `<stream>.jsonl.idx` (every INDEX_CADENCE'th seq → byte
340	 * offset) so tail-N reads can seek directly. The index is opportunistic
341	 * — readers must tolerate it being absent or stale.
342	 *
343	 * Acquires both the in-process chain and the on-disk lock.
344	 */
345	export async function appendArtifactLine(
346	  location: ArtifactStreamLocation,
347	  serializedLine: string,
348	  options: { seq?: number } = {},
349	): Promise<void> {
350	  await runOnArtifactChain(location.id, () =>
351	    withArtifactFileLock(location, async () => {
352	      // If a previous compaction stranded the plaintext under .gz, expand
353	      // back before appending so the new bytes are atomically appended to
354	      // the live transcript and not lost on the next read. expand() also
355	      // rebuilds the sparse index from scratch.
356	      await expandArtifactStreamInternal(location);
357	
358	      const guard = await needsLeadingNewline(location.filePath);
359	      const line = serializedLine.endsWith("\n") ? serializedLine : `${serializedLine}\n`;
360	      const writePayload = guard ? `\n${line}` : line;
361	
362	      // Capture the byte offset where the line *starts* — that's what
363	      // the index points to. After a guard newline we're one byte
364	      // further in.
365	      const preStat = await readFileState(location.filePath);
366	      const preSize = preStat?.size ?? 0;
367	      const lineStartOffset = preSize + (guard ? 1 : 0);
368	
369	      const handle = await fs.open(location.filePath, "a");
370	      try {
371	        await handle.appendFile(writePayload, "utf8");
372	        await handle.sync();
373	      } finally {
374	        await handle.close();
375	      }
376	
377	      if (options.seq != null && shouldIndex(options.seq)) {
378	        await appendIndexEntry(location, { seq: options.seq, offset: lineStartOffset });
379	      }
380	    }),
381	  );
382	}
383	
384	// --- Read: all entries ---------------------------------------------
385	
386	/**
387	 * Return all records currently durable on disk (plaintext first, then
388	 * gzip fallback). Callers that need legacy fallbacks (archive zip, DB
389	 * column, project-local → legacy global) should layer them above this.
390	 */
391	export async function readAllArtifactEntries<T>(location: ArtifactStreamLocation): Promise<T[]> {
392	  try {
393	    const body = await fs.readFile(location.filePath, "utf8");
394	    if (body.trim()) {
395	      return parseJsonlLines<T>(body);
396	    }
397	  } catch (error) {
398	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") throw error;
399	  }
400	  try {
401	    const buf = await fs.readFile(location.compressedFilePath);
402	    return parseJsonlLines<T>(gunzipSync(buf).toString("utf8"));
403	  } catch (error) {
404	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return [];
405	    throw error;
406	  }
407	}
408	
409	// --- Read: latest seq tail-scan ------------------------------------
410	
411	export interface SeqExtractor<T> {
412	  (line: string): { parsed: T | null; seq: number };
413	}
414	
415	const DEFAULT_MAX_TAIL_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;
416	const DEFAULT_CHUNK_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
417	
418	/**
419	 * Walk the plaintext file backward chunk-by-chunk until the highest
420	 * monotonic seq is found. Returns `null` when the boundary cannot be
421	 * proven (legacy entry without seq, file is gzipped only, etc.) — the
422	 * caller should fall back to a full read.
423	 */
424	export async function readLatestSeqFromTail<T>(
425	  location: ArtifactStreamLocation,
426	  extractor: SeqExtractor<T>,
427	  options: ReadEntriesSinceOptions = {},
428	): Promise<number | null> {
429	  const state = await readFileState(location.filePath);
430	  if (!state || state.size <= 0) return null;
431	
432	  const maxBytes = Math.min(state.size, options.maxBytes ?? DEFAULT_MAX_TAIL_BYTES);
433	  const chunkSize = Math.min(maxBytes, options.chunkSize ?? DEFAULT_CHUNK_BYTES);
434	  const handle = await fs.open(location.filePath, "r");
435	  try {
436	    let offset = state.size;
437	    let tail = "";
438	    while (offset > 0 && Buffer.byteLength(tail, "utf8") < maxBytes) {
439	      const readSize = Math.min(chunkSize, offset);
440	      offset -= readSize;
441	      const buffer = Buffer.alloc(readSize);
442	      await handle.read(buffer, 0, readSize, offset);
443	      tail = buffer.toString("utf8") + tail;
444	
445	      const lines = tail.split("\n");
446	      const firstLineIndex = offset === 0 ? 0 : 1;
447	      for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= firstLineIndex; i -= 1) {
448	        const trimmed = lines[i]?.trim();
449	        if (!trimmed) continue;
450	        const { seq } = extractor(trimmed);
451	        if (seq > 0) return seq;
452	        // A non-positive seq is the cursor boundary signal — the
453	        // adapter decides whether to treat that as "bail to full read".
454	        // Returning null here keeps that policy in one place.
455	        return null;
456	      }
457	    }
458	    return null;
459	  } finally {
460	    await handle.close();
461	  }
462	}
463	
464	/**
465	 * Walk the plaintext tail and collect records whose seq is strictly
466	 * greater than `afterSeq`, in ascending order. Returns `null` to signal
467	 * the caller should fall back to a full read (e.g. a non-monotonic
468	 * line was encountered before the boundary).
469	 */
470	export async function readEntriesSinceTail<T>(
471	  location: ArtifactStreamLocation,
472	  afterSeq: number,
473	  extractor: SeqExtractor<T>,
474	  options: ReadEntriesSinceOptions = {},
475	): Promise<{ entries: T[]; latestSeq: number } | null> {
476	  const state = await readFileState(location.filePath);
477	  if (!state || state.size <= 0) return null;
478	
479	  const maxBytes = Math.min(state.size, options.maxBytes ?? DEFAULT_MAX_TAIL_BYTES);
480	  const chunkSize = Math.min(maxBytes, options.chunkSize ?? DEFAULT_CHUNK_BYTES);
481	  const handle = await fs.open(location.filePath, "r");
482	  try {
483	    let offset = state.size;
484	    let tail = "";
485	    while (offset > 0 && Buffer.byteLength(tail, "utf8") < maxBytes) {
486	      const readSize = Math.min(chunkSize, offset);
487	      offset -= readSize;
488	      const buffer = Buffer.alloc(readSize);
489	      await handle.read(buffer, 0, readSize, offset);
490	      tail = buffer.toString("utf8") + tail;
491	
492	      const result = collectSinceInTail<T>(tail, offset === 0, afterSeq, extractor);
493	      if (result.complete) {
494	        return { entries: result.entries, latestSeq: result.latestSeq };
495	      }
496	    }
497	    return null;
498	  } finally {
499	    await handle.close();
500	  }
501	}

503	function collectSinceInTail<T>(
504	  text: string,
505	  includesFileStart: boolean,
506	  afterSeq: number,
507	  extractor: SeqExtractor<T>,
508	) {
509	  const lines = text.split("\n");
510	  const firstLineIndex = includesFileStart ? 0 : 1;
511	  const entries: T[] = [];
512	  let latestSeq = 0;
513	
514	  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= firstLineIndex; i -= 1) {
515	    const trimmed = lines[i]?.trim();
516	    if (!trimmed) continue;
517	    const { parsed, seq } = extractor(trimmed);
518	    if (seq <= 0 || parsed === null) {
519	      // Cursor boundary unprovable from the tail; caller falls back.
520	      return { complete: false, entries: [], latestSeq: 0 };
521	    }
522	    if (latestSeq === 0) latestSeq = seq;
523	    if (seq <= afterSeq) {
524	      entries.reverse();
525	      return { complete: true, entries, latestSeq };
526	    }
527	    entries.push(parsed);
528	  }
529	  if (includesFileStart) {
530	    entries.reverse();
531	    return { complete: true, entries, latestSeq };
532	  }
533	  return { complete: false, entries: [], latestSeq: 0 };
534	}
535	
536	// --- Compaction ----------------------------------------------------
537	
538	let tmpCounter = 0;
539	
540	async function expandArtifactStreamInternal(location: ArtifactStreamLocation): Promise<boolean> {
541	  let body: Buffer;
542	  try {
543	    body = await fs.readFile(location.compressedFilePath);
544	  } catch (error) {
545	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return false;
546	    throw error;
547	  }
548	  const decompressed = gunzipSync(body);
549	  tmpCounter = (tmpCounter + 1) >>> 0;
550	  const tmp = `${location.filePath}.tmp-${process.pid}-${Date.now()}-${tmpCounter}`;
551	  try {
552	    await fs.writeFile(tmp, decompressed);
553	    await fs.rename(tmp, location.filePath);
554	  } catch (error) {
555	    fs.unlink(tmp).catch(() => undefined);
556	    throw error;
557	  }
558	  await fs.unlink(location.compressedFilePath).catch(() => undefined);
559	  // The index was deleted on compact; rebuild it now that the plaintext
560	  // is back. Failure here is non-fatal — readers fall back to scan.
561	  try {
562	    await rebuildIndex(location);
563	  } catch {
564	    /* best-effort */
565	  }
566	  return true;
567	}
568	
569	async function compactArtifactStreamInternal(location: ArtifactStreamLocation): Promise<boolean> {
570	  let body: Buffer;
571	  try {
572	    body = await fs.readFile(location.filePath);
573	  } catch (error) {
574	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return false;
575	    throw error;
576	  }
577	  tmpCounter = (tmpCounter + 1) >>> 0;
578	  const tmp = `${location.compressedFilePath}.tmp-${process.pid}-${Date.now()}-${tmpCounter}`;
579	  const compressed = gzipSync(body);
580	  try {
581	    await fs.writeFile(tmp, compressed);
582	    await fs.rename(tmp, location.compressedFilePath);
583	  } catch (error) {
584	    fs.unlink(tmp).catch(() => undefined);
585	    throw error;
586	  }
587	  await fs.unlink(location.filePath).catch(() => undefined);
588	  // Index offsets are into the plaintext file that no longer exists.
589	  await deleteIndex(location);
590	  return true;
591	}
592	
593	/** Public compact entry point — acquires chain + lock. */
594	export async function compactArtifactStream(location: ArtifactStreamLocation): Promise<boolean> {
595	  return runOnArtifactChain(location.id, () => {
596	    if (!existsSync(location.filePath)) return Promise.resolve(false);
597	    return withArtifactFileLock(location, () => compactArtifactStreamInternal(location));
598	  });
599	}
600	
601	/** Public expand entry point — acquires chain + lock. */
602	export async function expandArtifactStream(location: ArtifactStreamLocation): Promise<boolean> {
603	  return runOnArtifactChain(location.id, () =>
604	    withArtifactFileLock(location, () => expandArtifactStreamInternal(location)),
605	  );
606	}
607	
608	// --- Delete --------------------------------------------------------
609	
610	export async function deleteArtifactStreamFiles(location: ArtifactStreamLocation): Promise<void> {
611	  await runOnArtifactChain(location.id, () =>
612	    withArtifactFileLock(location, async () => {
613	      for (const target of [location.filePath, location.compressedFilePath]) {
614	        try {
615	          await fs.unlink(target);
616	        } catch (error) {
617	          if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") throw error;
618	        }
619	      }
620	      await deleteIndex(location);
621	    }),
622	  );
623	}
624	
625	// --- Index-aware tail-N read ---------------------------------------
626	
627	/**
628	 * Read the last `limit` entries from the plaintext stream using the
629	 * sparse index when available. Falls back to `null` when the boundary
630	 * can't be proven from a fast seek (no index, stale index, legacy
631	 * pre-seq lines in the indexed region, gzipped-only stream).
632	 *
633	 * Callers can fall back to the slower backward chunk scan in that case.
634	 */
635	export async function readEntriesTailWithIndex<T>(
636	  location: ArtifactStreamLocation,
637	  latestSeq: number,
638	  limit: number,
639	  parseEnvelope: (line: string) => T | null,
640	): Promise<T[] | null> {
641	  if (limit <= 0 || latestSeq <= 0) return [];
642	
643	  const index = await readIndex(location);
644	  // Want the largest indexed seq strictly below (latestSeq - limit + 1).
645	  // That gives us a seek point from which we can scan forward and still
646	  // collect at least `limit` records (plus a few extras we discard).
647	  const targetSeq = Math.max(1, latestSeq - limit);
648	  const seekPoint = findIndexPointForSeq(index, targetSeq);
649	  if (!seekPoint) return null;
650	
651	  const fileState = await readFileState(location.filePath);
652	  if (!fileState || fileState.size <= seekPoint.offset) return null;
653	
654	  // Read everything from the seek point to EOF in one shot. For a 250K
655	  // file with index every 100 records this is at most ~30K bytes of
656	  // forward read — a single sequential I/O.
657	  const handle = await fs.open(location.filePath, "r");
658	  let text: string;
659	  try {
660	    const readLength = fileState.size - seekPoint.offset;
661	    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(readLength);
662	    await handle.read(buffer, 0, readLength, seekPoint.offset);
663	    text = buffer.toString("utf8");
664	  } finally {
665	    await handle.close();
666	  }
667	
668	  // First line in `text` is the record whose offset is seekPoint.offset
669	  // (i.e. seq === seekPoint.seq). Parse forward and keep the last
670	  // `limit` records.
671	  const entries: T[] = [];
672	  for (const line of text.split("\n")) {
673	    const trimmed = line.trim();
674	    if (!trimmed) continue;
675	    const parsed = parseEnvelope(trimmed);
676	    if (parsed === null) continue;
677	    entries.push(parsed);
678	  }
679	  if (entries.length === 0) return null;
680	  return entries.length > limit ? entries.slice(-limit) : entries;
681	}

1	/**
2	 * One-shot: rebuild the sparse seq→offset index for every worker_entries
3	 * artifact stream. Used after the legacy-runtime-output backfill so the
4	 * old transcripts get fast tail reads too.
5	 *
6	 * Usage: pnpm exec tsx scripts/rebuild-worker-indices.ts [--verbose]
7	 */
8	import path from "node:path";
9	import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
10	import { db } from "@/server/db";
11	import { artifactStreams, runs } from "@/server/db/schema";
12	import { resolveArtifactStreamLocation } from "@/server/artifacts/append-only-store";
13	import type { ArtifactStreamKind } from "@/server/artifacts/stream-types";
14	import { rebuildIndex } from "@/server/artifacts/stream-index";
15	
16	async function main() {
17	  const verbose = process.argv.includes("--verbose") || process.argv.includes("-v");
18	  const rows = await db.select().from(artifactStreams);
19	  const projectByRun = new Map<string, string | null>(
20	    (await db.select({ id: runs.id, projectPath: runs.projectPath }).from(runs))
21	      .map((r) => [r.id, r.projectPath ?? null]),
22	  );
23	
24	  let scanned = 0;
25	  let rebuilt = 0;
26	  let missing = 0;
27	  let failed = 0;
28	  for (const row of rows) {
29	    if (row.kind !== "worker_entries") continue;
30	    scanned += 1;
31	    const projectPath = projectByRun.get(row.runId) ?? null;
32	    let location;
33	    try {
34	      location = await resolveArtifactStreamLocation(
35	        {
36	          runId: row.runId,
37	          kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
38	          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
39	          projectPath,
40	        },
41	        "read",
42	      );
43	    } catch (error) {
44	      failed += 1;
45	      console.error(`[rebuild] ${row.runId}/${row.ownerId}: resolve failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : error}`);
46	      continue;
47	    }
48	    if (!existsSync(location.filePath)) {
49	      missing += 1;
50	      if (verbose) console.log(`[skip] ${row.runId}/${row.ownerId}: file missing`);
51	      continue;
52	    }
53	    try {
54	      const count = await rebuildIndex(location);
55	      rebuilt += 1;
56	      if (verbose) {
57	        console.log(`[rebuilt] ${row.runId}/${row.ownerId}: ${count} index entries at ${path.basename(location.filePath)}.idx`);
58	      }
59	    } catch (error) {
60	      failed += 1;
61	      console.error(`[rebuild] ${row.runId}/${row.ownerId}: failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : error}`);
62	    }
63	  }
64	  console.log(`[summary] scanned=${scanned} rebuilt=${rebuilt} missing=${missing} failed=${failed}`);
65	}
66	
67	main().catch((error) => {
68	  console.error(error);
69	  process.exit(1);
70	});
71

479	  } else if (readEntriesByKey.size >= READ_ENTRIES_CACHE_MAX) {

529	function runOnChain<T>(runId: string, workerId: string, task: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
530	  const key = chainKey(runId, workerId);
531	  const previous = writeChainByKey.get(key) ?? Promise.resolve();
532	  const next = previous.then(() => task());
533	  const tracked = next.then(() => undefined, () => undefined);
534	  writeChainByKey.set(key, tracked);
535	  return next.finally(() => {
536	    if (writeChainByKey.get(key) === tracked) {
537	      writeChainByKey.delete(key);
538	    }
539	  });
540	}

542	function clearChainCaches(runId: string, workerId: string) {

545	  seenIdsByKey.delete(key);
546	  fingerprintsByKey.delete(key);
547	  fileStateByKey.delete(key);
548	  readLatestSeqByKey.delete(key);
549	  readEntriesByKey.delete(key);

552	function workerFileLockDelay(attempt: number) {

554	  return Math.min(Math.round(delay), WORKER_FILE_LOCK_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS);

557	function sleep(ms: number) {

561	function isRecoverableLockRaceError(error: unknown) {
562	  const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
563	  return code === "ENOENT" || code === "ENOTDIR" || code === "EINVAL";
564	}

566	async function isWorkerFileLockStale(lockPath: string) {
567	  try {
568	    const stat = await fs.stat(lockPath);
569	    try {
570	      await fs.access(path.join(lockPath, "owner.json"));
571	    } catch (error) {
572	      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
573	        return true;
574	      }
575	      throw error;
576	    }
577	    return stat.mtimeMs < Date.now() - WORKER_FILE_LOCK_STALE_MS;
578	  } catch (error) {
579	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
580	      return true;
581	    }
582	    throw error;
583	  }
584	}

586	async function acquireWorkerFileLock(lockPath: string): Promise<() => Promise<void>> {
587	  const ownerPath = path.join(lockPath, "owner.json");
588	  const ownerToken = randomUUID();
589	  const owner = JSON.stringify({
590	    token: [REDACTED]
591	    pid: process.pid,
592	    createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
593	  });
594	
595	  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= WORKER_FILE_LOCK_RETRIES; attempt += 1) {
596	    try {
597	      await fs.mkdir(lockPath);
598	      try {
599	        await fs.writeFile(ownerPath, owner, "utf8");
600	      } catch (error) {
601	        await fs.rm(lockPath, { recursive: true, force: true });
602	        if (isRecoverableLockRaceError(error)) {
603	          continue;
604	        }
605	        throw error;
606	      }
607	
608	      let released = false;
609	      const refresh = async () => {
610	        if (released) {
611	          return;
612	        }
613	        const now = new Date();
614	        await fs.utimes(lockPath, now, now);
615	        await fs.utimes(ownerPath, now, now);
616	      };
617	      const interval = setInterval(() => {
618	        void refresh().catch(() => {});
619	      }, WORKER_FILE_LOCK_UPDATE_MS);
620	      interval.unref?.();
621	
622	      return async () => {
623	        if (released) {
624	          return;
625	        }
626	        released = true;
627	        clearInterval(interval);
628	        try {
629	          const currentOwner = await fs.readFile(ownerPath, "utf8");
630	          if (currentOwner !== owner) {
631	            return;
632	          }
633	        } catch (error) {
634	          if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
635	            return;
636	          }
637	          throw error;
638	        }
639	        await fs.rm(lockPath, { recursive: true, force: true });
640	      };
641	    } catch (error) {
642	      const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
643	      if (code !== "EEXIST") {
644	        throw error;
645	      }
646	
647	      if (await isWorkerFileLockStale(lockPath)) {
648	        await fs.rm(lockPath, { recursive: true, force: true });
649	        continue;
650	      }
651	
652	      if (attempt === WORKER_FILE_LOCK_RETRIES) {
653	        throw Object.assign(new Error(`Timed out waiting for worker output lock: ${lockPath}`), {
654	          code: "ELOCKED",
655	        });
656	      }
657	
658	      await sleep(workerFileLockDelay(attempt));
659	    }
660	  }
661	
662	  throw Object.assign(new Error(`Timed out waiting for worker output lock: ${lockPath}`), {
663	    code: "ELOCKED",
664	  });
665	}

667	async function withWorkerFileLock<T>(
668	  runId: string,
669	  workerId: string,
670	  task: (paths: WorkerStreamPaths) => Promise<T>,
671	): Promise<T> {
672	  const paths = await workerStreamPaths(runId, workerId, "write");
673	  await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(paths.filePath), { recursive: true });
674	  // Appending an empty string with `a` is an atomic touch.
675	  await fs.writeFile(paths.filePath, "", { flag: "a" });
676	  const release = await acquireWorkerFileLock(paths.lockPath);
677	  try {
678	    return await task(paths);
679	  } finally {
680	    await release();
681	  }
682	}

684	async function readWorkerFileState(runId: string, workerId: string) {
685	  const paths = await workerStreamPaths(runId, workerId, "read");
686	  try {
687	    const stat = await fs.stat(paths.filePath);
688	    return { size: stat.size, mtimeMs: stat.mtimeMs };
689	  } catch (error) {
690	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
691	      return { size: 0, mtimeMs: 0 };
692	    }
693	    throw error;
694	  }
695	}

697	async function refreshChainCaches(runId: string, workerId: string): Promise<{ nextSeq: number; seen: Set<string>; fingerprints: Map<string, string> }> {
698	  const key = chainKey(runId, workerId);
699	  const currentFileState = await readWorkerFileState(runId, workerId);
700	  const cachedNextSeq = nextSeqByKey.get(key);
701	  const cachedSeen = seenIdsByKey.get(key);
702	  const cachedFingerprints = fingerprintsByKey.get(key);
703	  const cachedFileState = fileStateByKey.get(key);
704	  if (
705	    cachedNextSeq !== undefined
706	    && cachedSeen
707	    && cachedFingerprints
708	    && cachedFileState
709	    && cachedFileState.size === currentFileState.size
710	    && cachedFileState.mtimeMs === currentFileState.mtimeMs
711	  ) {
712	    // Touch the LRU so an actively-used chain stays resident.
713	    rememberChainKey(key);
714	    nextSeqByKey.set(key, cachedNextSeq);
715	    seenIdsByKey.set(key, cachedSeen);
716	    fingerprintsByKey.set(key, cachedFingerprints);
717	    fileStateByKey.set(key, cachedFileState);
718	    return {
719	      nextSeq: cachedNextSeq,
720	      seen: cachedSeen,
721	      fingerprints: cachedFingerprints,
722	    };
723	  }

725	  chainCacheDiskRefreshesForTests += 1;
726	  // Use RAW persisted entries (pre-dedupe, pre-renumber) for the seq cursor
727	  // so we never advance backward. A previous in-disk corruption (e.g.
728	  // duplicate seqs from a cross-process race) used to be "corrected" by
729	  // normalizeWorkerEntrySeqs renumbering from 1, which then caused the
730	  // writer to land on seqs already present on disk — making the dupe
731	  // problem self-reinforcing. Read dedup signals (seen ids, fingerprints)
732	  // from the canonicalized view, but take maxSeq from the raw stream.
733	  const rawExisting = await readAllPersistedEntries(runId, workerId);
734	  let rawMaxSeq = 0;
735	  for (const entry of rawExisting) {
736	    if (typeof entry.seq === "number" && Number.isFinite(entry.seq) && entry.seq > rawMaxSeq) {
737	      rawMaxSeq = entry.seq;
738	    }
739	  }
740	  const canonical = normalizePersistedEntries(rawExisting);
741	  const seen = new Set<string>();
742	  const fingerprints = new Map<string, string>();
743	  for (const entry of canonical) {
744	    if (typeof entry.id === "string" && entry.id) {

748	  }

750	  // successful commit, so consulting it ensures we never reuse a seq another

753	  try {
754	    const { readArtifactStreamMetadata } = await import("@/server/artifacts/stream-metadata");
755	    const metadata = await readArtifactStreamMetadata({
756	      runId,
757	      kind: "worker_entries",
758	      ownerId: workerId,
759	    });
760	    if (metadata && typeof metadata.latestSeq === "number" && metadata.latestSeq > 0) {
761	      dbLatestSeq = metadata.latestSeq;
762	    }
763	  } catch {
764	    // Best-effort — if the metadata read fails, fall back to the file-only
765	    // cursor. The file lock still serializes within a process.
766	  }
767	  const nextSeq = Math.max(rawMaxSeq, dbLatestSeq) + 1;
768	  rememberChainKey(key);
769	  nextSeqByKey.set(key, nextSeq);
770	  seenIdsByKey.set(key, seen);
771	  fingerprintsByKey.set(key, fingerprints);
772	  fileStateByKey.set(key, await readWorkerFileState(runId, workerId));
773	  return { nextSeq, seen, fingerprints };

780	async function readAllPersistedEntries(runId: string, workerId: string): Promise<WorkerEntry[]> {

813	/**
814	 * Append a single worker entry to the JSONL file. The writer assigns

816	 * use). Acquires the per-worker chain so it cannot interleave with
817	 * compaction/expand/delete.
818	 *
819	 * If `entry.id` is already present on disk (or in the seen-ids cache),
820	 * the call is a no-op and the previously persisted entry is returned
821	 * with `appended: false` so wake-up publishers do not re-announce old seqs.
822	 */

824	  entry: WorkerEntry;
825	  appended: boolean;

828	export async function appendWorkerEntryWithResult(
829	  runId: string,
830	  workerId: string,
831	  entry: Omit<WorkerEntry, "seq">,
832	): Promise<AppendWorkerEntryResult> {

834	    return withWorkerFileLock(runId, workerId, async (paths) => {
835	      // If a compaction race somehow stranded the plaintext file under .gz,
836	      // expand it first so cache refresh sees the live transcript rather

838	      await expandWorkerOutputFileInternal(paths);
839	
840	      const { nextSeq, seen, fingerprints } = await refreshChainCaches(runId, workerId);
841	      if (entry.id && seen.has(entry.id)) {
842	        // Already persisted; load it back so the caller has a stable
843	        // record. Linear scan is fine: this is the dedup path and runs at
844	        // append cadence, not read cadence.
845	        const persisted = await readCanonicalPersistedEntries(runId, workerId);
846	        const match = persisted.find((line) => line.id === entry.id);
847	        if (match && typeof match.seq === "number") {
848	          return { entry: match, appended: false };
849	        }
850	        // Legacy line without seq: assign one virtually based on file
851	        // position. The writer doesn't advance nextSeq in this case.
852	        return { entry: { ...(entry as WorkerEntry), seq: 0 }, appended: false };
853	      }
854	
855	      const persistedEntry: WorkerEntry = {
856	        ...(entry as WorkerEntry),
857	        seq: nextSeq,
858	      };
859	      const compact = compactEntryForHistory(persistedEntry as unknown as CompactableEntry) as unknown as WorkerEntry;
860	      const line = JSON.stringify(compact) + "\n";
861	
862	      const target = paths.filePath;
863	      const newlineGuard = await needsLeadingNewline(target);
864	      // Capture pre-append size so we can record the byte offset of the
865	      // new line in the sparse seq→offset index. The newline-guard byte

868	      let sizeBefore = 0;
869	      try {
870	        sizeBefore = (await fs.stat(target)).size;
871	      } catch (error) {
872	        if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") throw error;
873	      }
874	      const lineStartOffset = sizeBefore + (newlineGuard ? 1 : 0);
875	      const handle = await fs.open(target, "a");
876	      try {
877	        await handle.appendFile(newlineGuard ? "\n" + line : line, "utf8");
878	        await handle.sync();
879	      } finally {
880	        await handle.close();
881	      }
882	
883	      if (shouldIndex(persistedEntry.seq)) {
884	        // Best-effort: appendIndexEntry swallows its own errors. The
885	        // index is opportunistic — a failure here only slows future tail
886	        // reads until the next rebuild.

889	          offset: lineStartOffset,

893	      if (entry.id) {

895	        fingerprints.set(entry.id, workerEntryFingerprint(compact));

897	      nextSeqByKey.set(chainKey(runId, workerId), nextSeq + 1);
898	      await rememberWorkerFileState(runId, workerId);
899	      const { commitArtifactAppend } = await import("@/server/artifacts/stream-metadata");
900	      await commitArtifactAppend({
901	        streamId: { runId, kind: "worker_entries", ownerId: workerId },
902	        seq: compact.seq,

1	/**
2	 * Resolves the artifact root for a run.
3	 *
4	 * Canonical location: `<run.projectPath>/.omniharness/run-data/<runId>/`
5	 *
6	 * Runs without `projectPath` (legacy data created before project paths
7	 * were tracked) fall back to the app-global `<appData>/run-data/<runId>/`
8	 * for *reads only*. New writes against a run with no project path are
9	 * rejected with a stable error code — callers must surface this to the
10	 * user rather than silently re-creating the legacy global mess.
11	 *
12	 * Stored SQLite metadata records the relative path under `.omniharness/run-data`
13	 * plus the absolute `projectPath`, never an absolute artifact path.
14	 * That keeps the data portable when a project moves on disk (e.g. the
15	 * user renames `~/work/foo` → `~/work/bar`).
16	 */
17	import path from "node:path";
18	import { promises as fs } from "node:fs";
19	import { getAppDataPath } from "@/server/app-root";
20	import { ensureProjectOmniharnessDir, getProjectOmniharnessDir } from "@/server/projects/config";
21	
22	const RUN_DATA_SUBDIR = "run-data";
23	const OMNIHARNESS_DIR = ".omniharness";
24	
25	export class ArtifactRootError extends Error {
26	  readonly code: string;
27	  constructor(message: string, code: string) {
28	    super(message);
29	    this.code = code;
30	    this.name = "ArtifactRootError";
31	  }
32	}
33	
34	export type ArtifactRootSource = "project" | "legacy_global";
35	
36	export interface ArtifactRoot {
37	  /** Absolute path of the run's artifact root directory. */
38	  absolutePath: string;
39	  /** Whether the root is project-local or the legacy global fallback. */
40	  source: ArtifactRootSource;
41	  /**
42	   * The `projectPath` recorded in SQLite metadata when writing artifacts.
43	   * null for legacy global roots (no owning project).
44	   */
45	  projectPath: string | null;
46	  /**
47	   * Relative path *of the run's artifact root* under either
48	   * `<project>/.omniharness/run-data/` or `<appData>/run-data/`. Stored
49	   * in SQLite metadata to keep records portable.
50	   */
51	  relativeRootPath: string;
52	}
53	
54	/**
55	 * Resolve the artifact root for a run from server-owned run metadata.
56	 * `projectPath` here is the value already on `runs.projectPath`; callers
57	 * MUST NOT accept it directly from client input.
58	 *
59	 * `mode`:
60	 *   - `read`: returns a project-local root if available, else falls back
61	 *     to the legacy global root (without creating anything).
62	 *   - `write`: refuses to resolve a legacy-global root. New writes must
63	 *     have an owning project. Returns project-local root and `mkdir -p`s
64	 *     it as a side effect.
65	 */
66	export async function resolveArtifactRoot(
67	  args: { runId: string; projectPath: string | null | undefined },
68	  mode: "read" | "write",
69	): Promise<ArtifactRoot> {
70	  const runId = args.runId?.trim();
71	  if (!runId) {
72	    throw new ArtifactRootError("Run id is required to resolve artifact root.", "runid_missing");
73	  }
74	
75	  const projectPath = args.projectPath?.trim() || null;
76	
77	  if (projectPath) {
78	    assertSafeRunId(runId);
79	    const projectRoot = path.resolve(projectPath);
80	    const omniDir = getProjectOmniharnessDir(projectRoot);
81	    const runRoot = path.join(omniDir, RUN_DATA_SUBDIR, runId);
82	
83	    if (mode === "write") {
84	      // If the project directory itself has gone (renamed, deleted, or
85	      // an in-test fake path), fall through to the legacy global root
86	      // rather than fail the whole append. The repair tool/backfill can
87	      // relocate once the project is back. We DON'T retry/create the
88	      // missing project root — that would silently scatter artifacts
89	      // through unrelated filesystems on misconfigured runs.
90	      try {
91	        ensureProjectOmniharnessDir(projectRoot);
92	        await fs.mkdir(runRoot, { recursive: true });
93	        return {
94	          absolutePath: runRoot,
95	          source: "project",
96	          projectPath: projectRoot,
97	          relativeRootPath: path.posix.join(RUN_DATA_SUBDIR, runId),
98	        };
99	      } catch (error) {
100	        const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
101	        if (code !== "ENOENT" && code !== "ENOTDIR") {
102	          throw error;
103	        }
104	        // fall through to legacy below
105	      }
106	    } else {
107	      return {
108	        absolutePath: runRoot,
109	        source: "project",
110	        projectPath: projectRoot,
111	        relativeRootPath: path.posix.join(RUN_DATA_SUBDIR, runId),
112	      };
113	    }
114	  }
115	
116	  // Legacy fallback: runs created before projectPath was a required
117	  // attribute land here. We let them keep writing to the app-global
118	  // run-data directory rather than fail the whole feature for old data.
119	  // Backfill can relocate them later. New runs SHOULD have projectPath
120	  // set so they end up project-local from the start.
121	  const legacyRoot = legacyGlobalRunRoot(runId);
122	  if (mode === "write") {
123	    await fs.mkdir(legacyRoot, { recursive: true });
124	  }
125	  return {
126	    absolutePath: legacyRoot,
127	    source: "legacy_global",
128	    projectPath: null,
129	    relativeRootPath: path.posix.join(RUN_DATA_SUBDIR, runId),
130	  };
131	}
132	
133	/**
134	 * Returns the absolute path of an artifact stream given the run's root
135	 * and a stream-relative path. The stream-relative path is what's stored
136	 * in `artifact_streams.relative_path` (e.g. `workers/abc-worker-1.jsonl`
137	 * or `execution-events.jsonl`). Hard-fails on path traversal or paths
138	 * that escape the artifact root.
139	 */
140	export function resolveStreamPathWithin(root: ArtifactRoot, relativeStreamPath: string): string {
141	  const normalized = path.posix.normalize(relativeStreamPath).replace(/^[/\\]+/, "");
142	  if (normalized.startsWith("..") || path.isAbsolute(normalized) || normalized.includes("\0")) {
143	    throw new ArtifactRootError(
144	      `Refusing artifact path that escapes its root: ${relativeStreamPath}`,
145	      "path_traversal",
146	    );
147	  }
148	  const absolute = path.join(root.absolutePath, normalized);
149	  // Belt-and-braces: ensure the resolved absolute path is still inside
150	  // the root after normalization.
151	  const rootResolved = path.resolve(root.absolutePath);
152	  const absResolved = path.resolve(absolute);
153	  if (absResolved !== rootResolved && !absResolved.startsWith(rootResolved + path.sep)) {
154	    throw new ArtifactRootError(
155	      `Refusing artifact path that escapes its root: ${relativeStreamPath}`,
156	      "path_traversal",
157	    );
158	  }
159	  return absResolved;
160	}
161	
162	function legacyGlobalRunRoot(runId: string) {
163	  return path.join(getAppDataPath(RUN_DATA_SUBDIR), runId);
164	}
165	
166	/**
167	 * The legacy global artifact root for a run. Used by readers that still
168	 * need to fall back to pre-migration files. New writes MUST NOT land here.
169	 */
170	export function legacyGlobalArtifactRoot(runId: string): ArtifactRoot {
171	  return {
172	    absolutePath: legacyGlobalRunRoot(runId),
173	    source: "legacy_global",
174	    projectPath: null,
175	    relativeRootPath: path.posix.join(RUN_DATA_SUBDIR, runId),
176	  };
177	}
178	
179	function assertSafeRunId(runId: string) {
180	  if (runId.includes("/") || runId.includes("\\") || runId.includes("..") || runId.includes("\0")) {
181	    throw new ArtifactRootError(
182	      `Refusing artifact root for unsafe run id: ${JSON.stringify(runId)}`,
183	      "unsafe_runid",
184	    );
185	  }
186	}
187	
188	export const ARTIFACT_DIR_NAME = OMNIHARNESS_DIR;
189	export const ARTIFACT_RUN_DATA_SUBDIR = RUN_DATA_SUBDIR;

2	 * Single source of truth for the unified worker conversation stream on
3	 * the frontend.
4	 *
5	 * Per (workerId) we hold a contiguous *window* [lowestSeq..latestContiguousSeq]:
6	 *   - entries: the contiguous window in seq order, never with gaps.
7	 *   - lowestSeq: the lowest seq currently in `entries` (0 if empty).
8	 *   - latestContiguousSeq: the highest seq we have proven contiguous
9	 *     from lowestSeq. Used as the cursor for forward refetch.
10	 *   - latestKnownSeq: the highest seq the server has told us exists.
11	 *     Updates immediately on a wake-up frame; the fetch fills the gap.
12	 *   - hasOlder: true if older entries exist on the server before
13	 *     lowestSeq. Set by initial tail-load and `loadOlder`.
14	 *   - status: "idle" → "loading" → "loaded"; "error" on a fetch failure.
15	 *
16	 * Initial load fetches the last N entries via `?limit=N`. Forward
17	 * extension uses `?afterSeq=latestContiguousSeq`. Backward hydration
18	 * uses `?beforeSeq=lowestSeq&limit=N` via `loadOlder`.
19	 *
20	 * SSE frames carry only `{ workerId, seq }` — the content is fetched
21	 * via the HTTP endpoint. The frame is a wake-up hint; we never trust
22	 * it as the entry payload.
23	 */

29	/**
30	 * Collapse multiple rows that share an entry `id` into a single
31	 * conversation item. The server's unified stream intentionally appends
32	 * a new row whenever an entry's text grows (so a streaming assistant
33	 * message can be revised in place — see the
34	 * `appends changed bridge message revisions so streaming prose can expand`
35	 * test in `tests/server/workers/output-store.test.ts`). It also
36	 * writes the same user_input id onto a newer worker's stream when a run
37	 * cycles through workers.
38	 *
39	 * Coalesce policy:
40	 *   - Keep the entry at its FIRST appearance in the input order, so
41	 *     conversational position doesn't jump when text grows.
42	 *   - Use the LATEST revision's text / metadata (text grows; latest
43	 *     revision is the finished one).
44	 *   - Take the timestamp from the copy on the NEWEST worker, because that
45	 *     is the one the live thread actually contains. Neither "earliest" nor
46	 *     "latest" works on its own: a rewind re-delivers a message with a new
47	 *     timestamp (newest is right, earliest pins it back above output it was
48	 *     rewound past), while `reconcileWorkerUserMessagesInStream` backfills
49	 *     history onto a fresh worker with the original `createdAt` (earliest is
50	 *     right, latest drags the opening prompt into the middle of the day).
51	 *     Worker order settles both. Copies from the same worker — streaming
52	 *     revisions, which share a timestamp anyway — keep the earliest.
53	 *   - Entries without an id pass through unchanged.
54	 *
55	 * `workerOrder` is the run's workers in creation order. Without it (a single
56	 * worker stream, or a caller that has no worker list yet) the earliest
57	 * timestamp is kept, which is the conservative choice: a message stays where
58	 * it already is.
59	 */
60	export function coalesceWorkerEntriesById(
61	  entries: ReadonlyArray<WorkerEntry>,
62	  workerOrder: ReadonlyArray<string> = [],
63	): WorkerEntry[] {
64	  const workerRank = new Map(workerOrder.map((workerId, index) => [workerId, index]));
65	  const rankOf = (entry: WorkerEntry) => {
66	    const workerId = (entry as { workerId?: unknown }).workerId;
67	    return typeof workerId === "string" ? workerRank.get(workerId) ?? -1 : -1;
68	  };
69	
70	  const positionByKey = new Map<string, number>();
71	  const placementByKey = new Map<string, { timestamp: string; rank: number }>();
72	  const result: WorkerEntry[] = [];
73	  for (const entry of entries) {
74	    const key = typeof entry.id === "string" && entry.id ? entry.id : null;
75	    if (!key) {
76	      result.push(entry);
77	      continue;
78	    }
79	    const existingPosition = positionByKey.get(key);
80	    if (existingPosition === undefined) {
81	      positionByKey.set(key, result.length);
82	      if (entry.timestamp) {
83	        placementByKey.set(key, { timestamp: entry.timestamp, rank: rankOf(entry) });
84	      }
85	      result.push(entry);
86	    } else {

89	      const candidateRank = rankOf(entry);

95	        const keepCandidate = candidateRank > held.rank

97	        preservedTimestamp = keepCandidate ? candidate : held.timestamp;
98	        placementByKey.set(key, {

102	      } else if (held) {

276	  getState(workerId: string, initialEntries: WorkerEntry[] = []): WorkerStreamState {

483	  private fetchTail(workerId: string, limit: number): Promise<void> {
484	    const existing = this.inFlightByWorker.get(workerId);
485	    if (existing) return existing;
486	    const previous = this.getState(workerId);
487	    this.updateState(workerId, { ...previous, status: "loading", lastError: null });
488	    const promise = this.load({ workerId, limit }).then(
489	      (response) => {
490	        const current = this.getState(workerId);
491	        const sorted = [...response.entries].sort((a, b) => a.seq - b.seq);
492	        const latestContiguous = sorted.length > 0 ? sorted[sorted.length - 1]!.seq : 0;
493	        const lowest = sorted.length > 0 ? sorted[0]!.seq : 0;
494	        // Preserve any latestKnownSeq advance that landed via wake-up
495	        // while this tail load was in flight.
496	        const currentKnown = current.needsTailValidation ? 0 : current.latestKnownSeq;
497	        const latestKnown = Math.max(currentKnown, response.latestSeq ?? 0, latestContiguous);
498	        this.updateState(workerId, {
499	          ...current,
500	          entries: sorted,
501	          lowestSeq: lowest,
502	          latestContiguousSeq: latestContiguous,
503	          latestKnownSeq: latestKnown,
504	          hasOlder: response.hasOlder ?? (lowest > 1),
505	          status: "loaded",
506	          lastError: null,
507	          needsTailValidation: false,
508	        });
509	      },
510	      (error: unknown) => {
511	        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
512	        const failing = this.getState(workerId);
513	        this.updateState(workerId, { ...failing, status: "error", lastError: message });
514	      },
515	    ).finally(() => {
516	      this.inFlightByWorker.delete(workerId);
517	      // If the server reported newer entries than we got in the tail
518	      // window, chase forward from latestContiguousSeq.
519	      const after = this.getState(workerId);
520	      if (after.status === "loaded" && after.latestContiguousSeq < after.latestKnownSeq) {
521	        void this.fetchForward(workerId, after.latestContiguousSeq);
522	      }
523	    });
524	    this.inFlightByWorker.set(workerId, promise);
525	    return promise;
526	  }

528	  private fetchBefore(workerId: string, beforeSeq: number, limit: number): Promise<void> {
529	    const existing = this.inFlightByWorker.get(workerId);
530	    if (existing) return existing;
531	    const previous = this.getState(workerId);
532	    this.updateState(workerId, { ...previous, status: "loading", lastError: null });
533	    const promise = this.load({ workerId, beforeSeq, limit }).then(
534	      (response) => {
535	        const current = this.getState(workerId);
536	        // Only accept entries strictly older than our current window and
537	        // adjacent to it (no gap to lowestSeq). If we'd introduce a gap,
538	        // drop the page — `loadOlder` can be retried.
539	        const sorted = [...response.entries]
540	          .filter((entry) => typeof entry.seq === "number" && entry.seq > 0 && entry.seq < current.lowestSeq)
541	          .sort((a, b) => a.seq - b.seq);
542	        if (sorted.length === 0) {
543	          this.updateState(workerId, {
544	            ...current,
545	            hasOlder: response.hasOlder ?? false,
546	            status: "loaded",
547	            lastError: null,
548	          });
549	          return;
550	        }
551	        const highestOlderSeq = sorted[sorted.length - 1]!.seq;
552	        if (current.lowestSeq > 0 && highestOlderSeq !== current.lowestSeq - 1) {
553	          // Gap — older page doesn't butt up to our window. Don't merge
554	          // (would violate the contiguity invariant). Still advance the
555	          // hasOlder hint if the server thinks there's nothing left.
556	          this.updateState(workerId, {
557	            ...current,
558	            hasOlder: response.hasOlder ?? current.hasOlder,
559	            status: "loaded",
560	            lastError: null,
561	          });
562	          return;
563	        }
564	        const lowest = sorted[0]!.seq;
565	        const merged = [...sorted, ...current.entries];
566	        this.updateState(workerId, {
567	          ...current,
568	          entries: merged,
569	          lowestSeq: lowest,
570	          hasOlder: response.hasOlder ?? (lowest > 1),
571	          status: "loaded",
572	          lastError: null,
573	        });
574	      },
575	      (error: unknown) => {
576	        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
577	        const failing = this.getState(workerId);
578	        this.updateState(workerId, { ...failing, status: "error", lastError: message });
579	      },
580	    ).finally(() => {
581	      this.inFlightByWorker.delete(workerId);
582	    });
583	    this.inFlightByWorker.set(workerId, promise);
584	    return promise;
585	  }

587	  private fetchForward(workerId: string, afterSeq: number): Promise<void> {
588	    const existing = this.inFlightByWorker.get(workerId);
589	    if (existing) {
590	      return existing;
591	    }
592	    const previous = this.getState(workerId);
593	    this.updateState(workerId, { ...previous, status: "loading", lastError: null });
594	    const cursorBeforeFetch = previous.latestContiguousSeq;
595	    const knownBeforeFetch = previous.latestKnownSeq;
596	    const wakeVersionBeforeFetch = this.wakeVersionByWorker.get(workerId) ?? 0;
597	    const promise = this.load({ workerId, afterSeq }).then(
598	      (response) => {
599	        this.applyFetchResult(workerId, afterSeq, response);
600	      },
601	      (error: unknown) => {
602	        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
603	        const failing = this.getState(workerId);
604	        this.updateState(workerId, { ...failing, status: "error", lastError: message });
605	      },
606	    ).finally(() => {
607	      this.inFlightByWorker.delete(workerId);
608	      // If applyFetchResult advanced the contiguous prefix and a known
609	      // gap remains, chase it now. Requiring progress prevents an
610	      // infinite loop when the server reports `latestSeq` ahead of the
611	      // entries it returned (race or stale latest hint).
612	      const after = this.getState(workerId);
613	      const wakeUpAdvancedKnownSeq = after.latestKnownSeq > knownBeforeFetch;
614	      const wakeUpArrivedDuringFetch = (this.wakeVersionByWorker.get(workerId) ?? 0) > wakeVersionBeforeFetch;
615	      if (
616	        after.status === "loaded"
617	        && (after.latestContiguousSeq > cursorBeforeFetch || wakeUpAdvancedKnownSeq || wakeUpArrivedDuringFetch)
618	        && after.latestContiguousSeq < after.latestKnownSeq
619	      ) {
620	        void this.fetchForward(workerId, after.latestContiguousSeq);
621	      }
622	    });
623	    this.inFlightByWorker.set(workerId, promise);
624	    return promise;
625	  }
626	
627	  private applyFetchResult(
628	    workerId: string,
629	    cursorBeforeFetch: number,
630	    response: FetchResponse,
631	  ): void {
632	    const previous = this.getState(workerId);
633	    // The endpoint returns entries strictly newer than `afterSeq`. If
634	    // the caller's view advanced between request and response, drop
635	    // anything we've already merged.
636	    const incoming = response.entries
637	      .filter((entry) => entry.seq > previous.latestContiguousSeq)
638	      .sort((a, b) => a.seq - b.seq);
639	
640	    let nextContiguous = previous.latestContiguousSeq;
641	    const merged = [...previous.entries];
642	    for (const entry of incoming) {
643	      if (entry.seq === nextContiguous + 1) {
644	        merged.push(entry);
645	        nextContiguous = entry.seq;
646	      } else if (entry.seq > nextContiguous + 1) {
647	        // Gap. Don't include the entry; the next forward load (kicked off
648	        // below) will cover both this seq and the missing ones.
649	        break;
650	      }
651	    }
652	
653	    const nextKnown = Math.max(previous.latestKnownSeq, response.latestSeq, nextContiguous);
654	    // If we started with no entries, lowestSeq becomes the first merged
655	    // entry's seq; otherwise the window's lower bound is unchanged.
656	    const nextLowest = previous.lowestSeq > 0
657	      ? previous.lowestSeq
658	      : merged[0]?.seq ?? 0;
659	    const next: WorkerStreamState = {
660	      ...previous,
661	      // Reuse the previous array when the poll appended nothing. The spread
662	      // above always allocates, so an idle validation poll used to hand every
663	      // subscriber a brand-new `entries` identity and invalidate each memo
664	      // derived from it — the transcript merge and Terminal's activity
665	      // rebuild both re-ran for a byte-identical result.
666	      entries: merged.length > previous.entries.length ? merged : previous.entries,
667	      lowestSeq: nextLowest,
668	      latestContiguousSeq: nextContiguous,
669	      latestKnownSeq: nextKnown,
670	      // hasOlder is preserved; only tail-load or loadOlder updates it.
671	      // A forward fetch starting from lowestSeq=0 (empty window) can't
672	      // assert anything about whether older entries exist.
673	      status: "loaded",
674	      lastError: null,
675	      needsTailValidation: false,
676	    };
677	    this.updateState(workerId, next);
678	
679	    // Gap chasing happens in the fetch wrapper's .finally so that
680	    // inFlightByWorker is cleared before the recursive call.
681	  }
682	
683	  private updateState(workerId: string, next: WorkerStreamState): void {
684	    this.stateByWorker.set(workerId, next);
685	    if (next.status === "loaded" && !next.needsTailValidation) {
686	      this.everLoadedWorkers.add(workerId);
687	    }
688	    if (next.status === "loaded") {
689	      this.rememberState(workerId, next.entries);
690	    }
691	    const listeners = this.listenersByWorker.get(workerId);
692	    if (!listeners) {
693	      return;
694	    }
695	    for (const listener of listeners) {
696	      listener(next);
697	    }
698	  }

700	  private getCachedEntries(workerId: string): WorkerEntry[] {
701	    const cached = this.readEnvelope().workers[workerId];
702	    if (!cached || !isWorkerEntryArray(cached.entries)) {
703	      return [];
704	    }
705	    // Trim to the tail window. The cache used to rehydrate full
706	    // transcripts which caused the worker view to render every entry
707	    // from seq 1 and then auto-scroll down — bad UX on long sessions.
708	    // We want the user to see the most recent N entries immediately,
709	    // then load older ones on scroll-back via loadOlder().
710	    if (cached.entries.length > DEFAULT_TAIL_LIMIT) {
711	      return cached.entries.slice(-DEFAULT_TAIL_LIMIT);
712	    }
713	    return cached.entries;
714	  }
715	
716	  private rememberState(workerId: string, entries: WorkerEntry[]): void {
717	    if (!this.storage) {

## Claude subagent agent-a97e3a4e0195cac4f: Claude tool result: toolu_01SWPAEYsoD1XjoghKwS4iT1 · 2026-08-03T17:47:41.252Z

```text
1	/**
2	 * Backfill the unified worker conversation stream from legacy
3	 * `.omniharness/agent-runtime-output/<workerId>.jsonl` files written
4	 * by the agent runtime's pre-cutover output archive.
5	 *
6	 * Sessions that ran before the worker conversation stream cutover never
7	 * had their bridge-produced entries (message / thought / tool_call /
8	 * tool_call_update / permission) routed through `appendWorkerEntry`.
9	 * The frontend now reads exclusively from the worker stream, so those
10	 * conversations appear empty in the UI even though the raw bridge
11	 * output is on disk.
12	 *
13	 * This script replays each runtime-output line through
14	 * `appendWorkerEntry`, which is idempotent (dedup by `entry.id`). Safe
15	 * to re-run.
16	 *
17	 * Usage:
18	 *   pnpm tsx scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts
19	 *   pnpm tsx scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts --dry-run
20	 *   pnpm tsx scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts --workerId <id>
21	 *   pnpm tsx scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts --verbose
22	 */
23	import fs from "fs";
24	import path from "path";
25	import readline from "readline";
26	import { db } from "@/server/db";
27	import { workers as workersTable } from "@/server/db/schema";
28	import { appendWorkerEntry } from "@/server/workers/output-store";
29	import type { BridgeWorkerEntryType, WorkerEntry } from "@/server/workers/entries-types";
30	
31	const BRIDGE_TYPES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set<BridgeWorkerEntryType>([
32	  "message",
33	  "thought",
34	  "tool_call",
35	  "tool_call_update",
36	  "permission",
37	]);
38	
39	interface Options {
40	  dryRun: boolean;
41	  workerId: string | null;
42	  verbose: boolean;
43	  runtimeOutputDir: string;
44	}
45	
46	interface FileStats {
47	  workerId: string;
48	  runId: string | null;
49	  totalLines: number;
50	  appended: number;
51	  skippedDuplicate: number;
52	  skippedNonBridge: number;
53	  malformed: number;
54	}
55	
56	function parseOptions(argv: string[]): Options {
57	  const opts: Options = {
58	    dryRun: false,
59	    workerId: null,
60	    verbose: false,
61	    runtimeOutputDir: path.resolve(process.cwd(), ".omniharness/agent-runtime-output"),
62	  };
63	  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 1) {
64	    const arg = argv[i];
65	    if (arg === "--dry-run") opts.dryRun = true;
66	    else if (arg === "--verbose") opts.verbose = true;
67	    else if (arg === "--workerId") opts.workerId = argv[++i] ?? null;
68	    else if (arg === "--runtime-output-dir") opts.runtimeOutputDir = path.resolve(argv[++i] ?? "");
69	    else if (arg === "--help" || arg === "-h") {
70	      console.log("Usage: pnpm tsx scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts [--dry-run] [--workerId <id>] [--verbose]");
71	      process.exit(0);
72	    }
73	  }
74	  return opts;
75	}
76	
77	async function processFile(
78	  filePath: string,
79	  workerId: string,
80	  runId: string,
81	  opts: Options,
82	): Promise<FileStats> {
83	  const stats: FileStats = {
84	    workerId,
85	    runId,
86	    totalLines: 0,
87	    appended: 0,
88	    skippedDuplicate: 0,
89	    skippedNonBridge: 0,
90	    malformed: 0,
91	  };
92	
93	  const rl = readline.createInterface({
94	    input: fs.createReadStream(filePath, { encoding: "utf8" }),
95	    crlfDelay: Infinity,
96	  });
97	
98	  for await (const line of rl) {
99	    if (!line.trim()) continue;
100	    stats.totalLines += 1;
101	
102	    let parsed: Record<string, unknown>;
103	    try {
104	      parsed = JSON.parse(line);
105	    } catch {
106	      stats.malformed += 1;
107	      continue;
108	    }
109	
110	    const type = parsed.type;
111	    if (typeof type !== "string" || !BRIDGE_TYPES.has(type)) {
112	      stats.skippedNonBridge += 1;
113	      continue;
114	    }
115	    const id = parsed.id;
116	    if (typeof id !== "string" || !id) {
117	      stats.malformed += 1;
118	      continue;
119	    }
120	    const timestamp = typeof parsed.timestamp === "string" ? parsed.timestamp : new Date().toISOString();
121	    const text = typeof parsed.text === "string" ? parsed.text : "";
122	
123	    if (opts.dryRun) {
124	      stats.appended += 1;
125	      continue;
126	    }
127	
128	    const entry: Omit<WorkerEntry, "seq"> = {
129	      id,
130	      type: type as BridgeWorkerEntryType,
131	      text,
132	      timestamp,
133	      toolCallId: typeof parsed.toolCallId === "string" ? parsed.toolCallId : undefined,
134	      toolKind: typeof parsed.toolKind === "string" ? parsed.toolKind : undefined,
135	      status: typeof parsed.status === "string" ? parsed.status : undefined,
136	      raw: parsed.raw,
137	    };
138	
139	    try {
140	      // appendWorkerEntry dedups by entry.id; replaying is safe.
141	      // We can't observe `appended` from this entrypoint, so we treat
142	      // any non-throwing call as success and post-tally with a count
143	      // delta below. For simplicity here we just count attempts; a
144	      // re-run reports the new dedup hits as `skippedDuplicate=0`
145	      // attempts because dedup happens server-side and is silent.
146	      await appendWorkerEntry(runId, workerId, entry);
147	      stats.appended += 1;
148	    } catch (error) {
149	      stats.malformed += 1;
150	      if (opts.verbose) {
151	        console.warn(`[backfill] ${workerId} line ${stats.totalLines} failed:`, error);
152	      }
153	    }
154	  }
155	
156	  return stats;
157	}
158	
159	async function main() {
160	  const opts = parseOptions(process.argv.slice(2));
161	
162	  if (!fs.existsSync(opts.runtimeOutputDir)) {
163	    console.error(`Runtime output dir not found: ${opts.runtimeOutputDir}`);
164	    process.exit(1);
165	  }
166	
167	  type WorkerRow = typeof workersTable.$inferSelect;
168	  const allWorkers = (await db.select().from(workersTable)) as WorkerRow[];
169	  const workerById = new Map<string, WorkerRow>(allWorkers.map((row) => [row.id, row]));
170	
171	  const files = fs.readdirSync(opts.runtimeOutputDir).filter((name) => name.endsWith(".jsonl"));
172	  const targets = opts.workerId
173	    ? files.filter((name) => name === `${opts.workerId}.jsonl`)
174	    : files;
175	
176	  if (targets.length === 0) {
177	    console.log("No matching runtime-output files.");
178	    return;
179	  }
180	
181	  const totals = {
182	    files: 0,
183	    skippedNoWorkerRow: 0,
184	    totalLines: 0,
185	    appended: 0,
186	    skippedNonBridge: 0,
187	    malformed: 0,
188	  };
189	
190	  for (const file of targets) {
191	    const workerId = file.replace(/\.jsonl$/, "");
192	    const workerRow = workerById.get(workerId);
193	    if (!workerRow) {
194	      totals.skippedNoWorkerRow += 1;
195	      if (opts.verbose) console.log(`[skip] no workers row for ${workerId}`);
196	      continue;
197	    }
198	    const stats = await processFile(
199	      path.join(opts.runtimeOutputDir, file),
200	      workerId,
201	      workerRow.runId,
202	      opts,
203	    );
204	    totals.files += 1;
205	    totals.totalLines += stats.totalLines;
206	    totals.appended += stats.appended;
207	    totals.skippedNonBridge += stats.skippedNonBridge;
208	    totals.malformed += stats.malformed;
209	    if (opts.verbose || stats.malformed > 0) {
210	      console.log(`[done] ${workerId}: ${JSON.stringify(stats)}`);
211	    }
212	  }
213	
214	  console.log("Backfill summary:");
215	  console.log(JSON.stringify({ ...totals, dryRun: opts.dryRun }, null, 2));
216	}
217	
218	main().catch((error) => {
219	  console.error(error);
220	  process.exit(1);
221	});
222	

uuid: 06bb4741-a8b4-483b-859f-db0f66d5503d
parent: 5db28d15-9346-4d27-b2b4-3f6bcb698940
```

79	// Sort comparator for the merged transcript. Primary key: timestamp ms
80	// (so user input lands next to the worker turn it triggered, even
81	// across workers). Secondary: worker creation order (older worker

83	function compareTranscriptEntries(

97	function latestReturnedSeq(entries: WorkerEntry[]) {

100	      ? Math.floor(entry.seq)
