```text
1	/**
2	 * Run-scoped sibling of `WorkerEntriesManager`. Fetches the merged
3	 * transcript across every worker in a run from
4	 * the typed conversation transcript API, so the conversation UI can
5	 * render full history when the run has cycled through multiple workers
6	 * (cancel + respawn).
7	 *
8	 * Pagination is token-based because seq is per-worker, not global. The
9	 * server hands back an opaque cursor; we hand it back on the next poll.
10	 */
11	import { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
12	import type { WorkerEntry } from "@/shared/worker-entries";
13	import { coalesceWorkerEntriesById } from "./WorkerEntriesManager";
14	import type { RuntimeAPIs } from "@/runtime-api/types";
15	import { useRuntimeAPIs } from "@/runtime-api/provider";
16	
17	export interface ConversationTranscriptEntry extends WorkerEntry {
18	  workerId: string;
19	}
20	
21	export interface ConversationTranscriptState {
22	  entries: ConversationTranscriptEntry[];
23	  latestToken: string | null;
24	  oldestToken: string | null;
25	  hasOlder: boolean;
26	  status: "idle" | "loading" | "loaded" | "error";
27	  lastError: string | null;
28	  workerIds: string[];
29	  /**
30	   * Latched: true once this run's transcript has loaded at least once.
31	   * `status` cycles back through "loading" on every poll refresh, so
32	   * render gates must use this instead of `status === "loaded"`.
33	   */
34	  hasLoadedOnce: boolean;
35	}
36	
37	interface TranscriptFetchResponse {
38	  entries: ConversationTranscriptEntry[];
39	  latestToken: string;
40	  oldestToken?: string;
41	  hasOlder?: boolean;
42	  workerIds: string[];
43	}
44	
45	const DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_LIMIT = 100;
46	
47	const EMPTY: ConversationTranscriptState = Object.freeze({
48	  entries: [],
49	  latestToken: null,
50	  oldestToken: null,
51	  hasOlder: false,
52	  status: "idle",
53	  lastError: null,
54	  workerIds: [],
55	  hasLoadedOnce: false,
56	});
57	
58	export const EMPTY_CONVERSATION_TRANSCRIPT_STATE = EMPTY;
59	
60	export interface ConversationTranscriptManagerOptions {
61	  transcript?: RuntimeAPIs["conversations"]["transcript"];
62	}
63	
64	export class ConversationTranscriptManager {
65	  private readonly stateByRunId = new Map<string, ConversationTranscriptState>();
66	  private readonly listenersByRunId = new Map<string, Set<() => void>>();
67	  private readonly inFlightByRunId = new Map<string, Promise<void>>();
68	  private transcript: RuntimeAPIs["conversations"]["transcript"] | null;
69	
70	  constructor(options: ConversationTranscriptManagerOptions = {}) {
71	    this.transcript = options.transcript ?? null;
72	  }
73	
74	  configure(transcript: RuntimeAPIs["conversations"]["transcript"]) {
75	    this.transcript = transcript;
76	  }
77	
78	  private load(input: Parameters<RuntimeAPIs["conversations"]["transcript"]>[0]) {
79	    if (!this.transcript) {
80	      return Promise.reject(new Error("Conversation transcripts are not connected to the runtime."));
81	    }
82	    return this.transcript(input) as Promise<TranscriptFetchResponse>;
83	  }
84	
85	  getState(runId: string): ConversationTranscriptState {
86	    return this.stateByRunId.get(runId) ?? EMPTY;
87	  }
88	
89	  subscribe(runId: string, listener: () => void): () => void {
90	    const listeners = this.listenersByRunId.get(runId) ?? new Set();
91	    listeners.add(listener);
92	    this.listenersByRunId.set(runId, listeners);
93	    return () => {
94	      const current = this.listenersByRunId.get(runId);
95	      if (!current) return;
96	      current.delete(listener);
97	      if (current.size === 0) {
98	        this.listenersByRunId.delete(runId);
99	      }
100	    };
101	  }
102	
103	  ensureLoaded(runId: string): Promise<void> {
104	    const state = this.getState(runId);
105	    if (state.status === "loaded" || state.status === "loading") {
106	      return this.inFlightByRunId.get(runId) ?? Promise.resolve();
107	    }
108	    return this.fetchTail(runId);
109	  }
110	
111	  refresh(runId: string): Promise<void> {
112	    if (this.inFlightByRunId.has(runId)) {
113	      return this.inFlightByRunId.get(runId)!;
114	    }
115	    const state = this.getState(runId);
116	    return state.latestToken ? this.fetchForward(runId, state.latestToken) : this.fetchTail(runId);
117	  }
118	
119	  loadOlder(runId: string, limit: number = DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_LIMIT): Promise<void> {
120	    if (this.inFlightByRunId.has(runId)) {
121	      return this.inFlightByRunId.get(runId)!;
122	    }
123	    const state = this.getState(runId);
124	    if (!state.hasOlder || !state.oldestToken) {
125	      return Promise.resolve();
126	    }
127	    return this.fetchOlder(runId, state.oldestToken, limit);
128	  }
129	
130	  reset(): void {
131	    this.stateByRunId.clear();
132	    this.inFlightByRunId.clear();
133	    this.listenersByRunId.clear();
134	  }
135	
136	  private updateState(runId: string, next: ConversationTranscriptState): void {
137	    this.stateByRunId.set(runId, next);
138	    const listeners = this.listenersByRunId.get(runId);
139	    if (listeners) {
140	      for (const listener of listeners) {
141	        listener();
142	      }
143	    }
144	  }
145	
146	  private async fetchTail(runId: string, limit: number = DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_LIMIT): Promise<void> {
147	    const previous = this.getState(runId);
148	    this.updateState(runId, { ...previous, status: "loading", lastError: null });
149	    const promise = this.load({ runId, limit }).then(
150	      (response) => {
151	        const current = this.getState(runId);
152	        const next: ConversationTranscriptState = {
153	          ...current,
154	          entries: coalesceWorkerEntriesById(response.entries) as ConversationTranscriptEntry[],
155	          latestToken: response.latestToken,
156	          oldestToken: response.oldestToken ?? null,
157	          hasOlder: Boolean(response.hasOlder),
158	          workerIds: response.workerIds,
159	          status: "loaded",
160	          lastError: null,
161	          hasLoadedOnce: true,
162	        };
163	        this.updateState(runId, next);
164	      },
165	      (error: unknown) => {
166	        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
167	        const failing = this.getState(runId);
168	        this.updateState(runId, { ...failing, status: "error", lastError: message });
169	      },
170	    ).finally(() => {
171	      this.inFlightByRunId.delete(runId);
172	    });
173	    this.inFlightByRunId.set(runId, promise);
174	    return promise;
175	  }
176	
177	  private async fetchForward(runId: string, latestToken: string): Promise<void> {
178	    const previous = this.getState(runId);
179	    this.updateState(runId, { ...previous, status: "loading", lastError: null });
180	    const promise = this.load({ runId, afterToken: latestToken }).then(
181	      (response) => {
182	        const current = this.getState(runId);
183	        const next: ConversationTranscriptState = {
184	          ...current,
185	          entries: coalesceWorkerEntriesById([...current.entries, ...response.entries]) as ConversationTranscriptEntry[],
186	          latestToken: response.latestToken,
187	          oldestToken: current.oldestToken ?? response.oldestToken ?? null,
188	          hasOlder: current.hasOlder || Boolean(response.hasOlder),
189	          workerIds: response.workerIds,
190	          status: "loaded",
191	          lastError: null,
192	          hasLoadedOnce: true,
193	        };
194	        this.updateState(runId, next);
195	      },
196	      (error: unknown) => {
197	        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
198	        const failing = this.getState(runId);
199	        this.updateState(runId, { ...failing, status: "error", lastError: message });
200	      },
201	    ).finally(() => {
202	      this.inFlightByRunId.delete(runId);
203	    });
204	    this.inFlightByRunId.set(runId, promise);
205	    return promise;
206	  }
207	
208	  private async fetchOlder(runId: string, oldestToken: string, limit: number): Promise<void> {
209	    const previous = this.getState(runId);
210	    this.updateState(runId, { ...previous, status: "loading", lastError: null });
211	    const promise = this.load({ runId, beforeToken: oldestToken, limit }).then(
212	      (response) => {
213	        const current = this.getState(runId);
214	        const next: ConversationTranscriptState = {
215	          ...current,
216	          entries: coalesceWorkerEntriesById([...response.entries, ...current.entries]) as ConversationTranscriptEntry[],
217	          latestToken: current.latestToken ?? response.latestToken,
218	          oldestToken: response.oldestToken ?? current.oldestToken,
219	          hasOlder: Boolean(response.hasOlder),
220	          workerIds: response.workerIds,
221	          status: "loaded",
222	          lastError: null,
223	          hasLoadedOnce: true,
224	        };
225	        this.updateState(runId, next);
226	      },
227	      (error: unknown) => {
228	        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
229	        const failing = this.getState(runId);
230	        this.updateState(runId, { ...failing, status: "error", lastError: message });
231	      },
232	    ).finally(() => {
233	      this.inFlightByRunId.delete(runId);
234	    });
235	    this.inFlightByRunId.set(runId, promise);
236	    return promise;
237	  }
238	}
239	
240	export const conversationTranscriptManager = new ConversationTranscriptManager();
241	
242	interface UseConversationTranscriptOptions {
243	  refreshIntervalMs?: number | null;
244	  enabled?: boolean;
245	}
246	
247	/**
248	 * Subscribe to the merged conversation transcript for a run. When
249	 * `runId` is null or `options.enabled` is false, returns an empty
250	 * state and skips the fetch.
251	 */
252	export function useConversationTranscript(
253	  runId: string | null,
254	  options: UseConversationTranscriptOptions = {},

1	/**
2	 * Run-scoped artifact cleanup. Used by conversation-delete server
3	 * paths and the delete-conversations shell script to remove every
4	 * artifact stream file belonging to a run, in both the project-local
5	 * `<project>/.omniharness/run-data/<runId>/` tree and the legacy
6	 * global `<appData>/run-data/<runId>/` tree.
7	 *
8	 * The SQL `artifact_streams` rows are cascade-deleted by the FK to
9	 * runs; this module handles the filesystem side.
10	 */
11	import { promises as fs } from "node:fs";
12	import path from "node:path";
13	import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
14	import { db } from "@/server/db";
15	import { runs } from "@/server/db/schema";
16	import { resolveArtifactRoot, legacyGlobalArtifactRoot } from "./project-root";
17	
18	export interface CleanupReport {
19	  removedDirs: string[];
20	  removedFiles: string[];
21	  errors: Array<{ path: string; error: string }>;
22	}
23	
24	/**
25	 * Remove every artifact file (plaintext, gzipped, lock, index) for a
26	 * run. Idempotent — missing files are ignored. Returns a report so
27	 * callers can log what was actually removed.
28	 *
29	 * The run row itself is NOT deleted by this helper. Callers that
30	 * delete the row should also call this; the order matters only for
31	 * tests that rely on the cascade — DB cascade only removes
32	 * `artifact_streams` rows, not the on-disk files.
33	 */
34	export async function cleanupRunArtifacts(runId: string): Promise<CleanupReport> {
35	  const report: CleanupReport = { removedDirs: [], removedFiles: [], errors: [] };
36	
37	  const run = await db.select({ projectPath: runs.projectPath }).from(runs).where(eq(runs.id, runId)).get();
38	  const candidates = new Set<string>();
39	
40	  // Project-local root (if any).
41	  if (run?.projectPath) {
42	    try {
43	      const root = await resolveArtifactRoot({ runId, projectPath: run.projectPath }, "read");
44	      candidates.add(root.absolutePath);
45	    } catch {
46	      // Project root may be unresolvable (project moved/deleted); fall
47	      // through and try the legacy global root.
48	    }
49	  }
50	
51	  // Legacy global root.
52	  candidates.add(legacyGlobalArtifactRoot(runId).absolutePath);
53	
54	  for (const dir of candidates) {
55	    try {
56	      await fs.rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
57	      report.removedDirs.push(dir);
58	    } catch (error) {
59	      const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
60	      if (code === "ENOENT") continue;
61	      report.errors.push({
62	        path: dir,
63	        error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
64	      });
65	    }
66	  }
67	
68	  // Also remove the legacy archive zip if present.
69	  try {
70	    const zip = path.join(path.dirname(legacyGlobalArtifactRoot(runId).absolutePath), `${runId}.zip`);
71	    await fs.unlink(zip);
72	    report.removedFiles.push(zip);
73	  } catch (error) {
74	    const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
75	    if (code !== "ENOENT") {
76	      report.errors.push({
77	        path: `${runId}.zip`,
78	        error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
79	      });
80	    }
81	  }
82	
83	  // Remove the agent runtime's per-worker output archive (a separate
84	  // store from the worker conversation stream). Files are named
85	  // `<runId>-worker-*.jsonl` under `.omniharness/agent-runtime-output/`.
86	  // The directory is resolved relative to process.cwd() to match
87	  // `openAgentOutputArchive` in src/server/agent-runtime/output-store.ts.
88	  const runtimeOutputDir = path.join(process.cwd(), ".omniharness", "agent-runtime-output");
89	  try {
90	    const entries = await fs.readdir(runtimeOutputDir);
91	    const prefix = `${runId}-`;
92	    for (const entry of entries) {
93	      if (!entry.startsWith(prefix) || !entry.endsWith(".jsonl")) continue;
94	      const filePath = path.join(runtimeOutputDir, entry);
95	      try {
96	        await fs.unlink(filePath);
97	        report.removedFiles.push(filePath);
98	      } catch (error) {
99	        const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
100	        if (code !== "ENOENT") {
101	          report.errors.push({
102	            path: filePath,
103	            error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
104	          });
105	        }
106	      }
107	    }
108	  } catch (error) {
109	    const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
110	    if (code !== "ENOENT") {
111	      report.errors.push({
112	        path: runtimeOutputDir,
113	        error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
114	      });
115	    }
116	  }
117	
118	  return report;
119	}
120	
121	/**
122	 * Bulk-cleanup helper: given a list of runIds, remove all artifact
123	 * data for each. Returns the per-runId report so the caller can log.
124	 */
125	export async function cleanupRunArtifactsBatch(runIds: string[]): Promise<Map<string, CleanupReport>> {
126	  const reports = new Map<string, CleanupReport>();
127	  for (const runId of runIds) {
128	    reports.set(runId, await cleanupRunArtifacts(runId));
129	  }
130	  return reports;
131	}

1	import type { WorkerStreamState } from "./WorkerEntriesManager";
2	import { coalesceWorkerEntriesById } from "./WorkerEntriesManager";
3	import type { WorkerEntry } from "@/shared/worker-entries";

5	
6	export type ConversationLoadState = {
7	  snapshotLoaded: boolean;
8	  workerStreamRequired: boolean;
9	  workerStreamLoaded: boolean;
10	  fullyLoaded: boolean;
11	  loadingReason: "snapshot" | "worker_stream" | null;
12	};
13	
14	export function isWorkerStreamCaughtUp(streamState: WorkerStreamState) {
15	  return (
16	    streamState.status === "loaded"
17	    && streamState.latestContiguousSeq === streamState.latestKnownSeq
18	  );
19	}
20	
21	export function deriveConversationLoadState(args: {
22	  snapshotLoaded: boolean;
23	  unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled: boolean;
24	  primaryConversationWorkerId: string | null | undefined;
25	  streamState: WorkerStreamState;
26	  selectedRunIsTerminal?: boolean;
27	}): ConversationLoadState {
28	  const workerStreamRequired = Boolean(
29	    args.unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled
30	      && args.primaryConversationWorkerId
31	      && !args.selectedRunIsTerminal
32	  );
33	  const workerStreamLoaded = !workerStreamRequired || isWorkerStreamCaughtUp(args.streamState);
34	  const fullyLoaded = args.snapshotLoaded && workerStreamLoaded;
35	  const loadingReason = !args.snapshotLoaded
36	    ? "snapshot"
37	    : !workerStreamLoaded
38	      ? "worker_stream"
39	      : null;
40	
41	  return {
42	    snapshotLoaded: args.snapshotLoaded,
43	    workerStreamRequired,
44	    workerStreamLoaded,
45	    fullyLoaded,
46	    loadingReason,
47	  };
48	}
49	
50	export function shouldShowDirectWorkerStreamInitialLoading(args: {
51	  unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled: boolean;
52	  primaryConversationWorkerId: string | null | undefined;
53	  streamState: WorkerStreamState;
54	}) {
55	  return deriveConversationLoadState({
56	    ...args,
57	    snapshotLoaded: true,
58	  }).loadingReason === "worker_stream"
59	    && (args.streamState.status === "idle" || args.streamState.status === "loading")
60	    && args.streamState.entries.length === 0;
61	}
62	
63	export function shouldShowDirectConversationLoading(args: ConversationLoadState) {
64	  return Boolean(
65	    !args.fullyLoaded
66	    && args.loadingReason === "worker_stream"
67	  );
68	}
69	
70	export function selectDirectConversationEntries<T extends WorkerEntry>(args: {
71	  transcriptEntries: T[];
72	  directWorkerEntries: T[];
73	  // Ranges the live worker wrote for a branch a retry/edit discarded. The
74	  // transcript already drops them server-side; the live stream is served from
75	  // the raw JSONL (no database read on that hot path), so they are filtered
76	  // here before the two sources are merged — otherwise the rewound turn walks
77	  // straight back into the conversation.
78	  supersededSeqRanges?: SupersededSeqRange[];
79	  // The run's workers in creation order, so a message that exists on more than
80	  // one of them is placed where the newest worker has it.
81	  workerOrder?: ReadonlyArray<string>;
82	}) {
83	  const directWorkerEntries = withoutSupersededEntries(
84	    args.directWorkerEntries,
85	    args.supersededSeqRanges ?? [],
86	  );
87	
88	  if (args.transcriptEntries.length === 0) {
89	    return directWorkerEntries;
90	  }
91	
92	  return coalesceWorkerEntriesById([
93	    ...args.transcriptEntries,
94	    ...directWorkerEntries,
95	  ], args.workerOrder ?? []) as T[];
96	}
97	
98	export function resolveDirectWorkerStreamRefreshInterval(args: {
99	  unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled: boolean;
100	  primaryConversationWorkerId: string | null | undefined;
101	  activeRefreshIntervalMs: number;
102	  validationIntervalMs: number;
103	  showDirectControlWorkingIndicator: boolean;
104	  selectedRunIsTerminal?: boolean;
105	}) {
106	  if (!args.unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled || !args.primaryConversationWorkerId) {
107	    return null;
108	  }
109	
110	  return args.showDirectControlWorkingIndicator
111	    ? args.activeRefreshIntervalMs
112	    : args.validationIntervalMs;

1	import { asc, eq } from "drizzle-orm";
2	import type { AgentRecord } from "@/server/bridge-client";
3	import { db } from "@/server/db";
4	import { messages, runs, workers } from "@/server/db/schema";
5	import { parseChatAttachmentsJson } from "@/lib/chat-attachments";
6	import { appendUserInputOnDelivery } from "@/server/workers/stream-writer";
7	import {
8	  parseLegacyOutputEntriesJson,
9	  readWorkerOutputEntries,
10	  writeWorkerOutputEntries,
11	} from "@/server/workers/output-store";
12	import { appendWorkerSessionMetadata } from "@/server/workers/session-metadata";
13	
14	type PersistableWorkerSnapshot = Pick<AgentRecord, "outputEntries" | "currentText" | "lastText"> & {
15	  sessionId?: string | null;
16	  sessionMode?: string | null;
17	};
18	
19	/**
20	 * Backward-compatible synchronous parser for legacy DB-stored JSON.
21	 * New code should call readWorkerOutputEntries(runId, workerId) instead.
22	 */
23	export function parseWorkerOutputEntries(value: string | null | undefined) {
24	  return parseLegacyOutputEntriesJson(value);
25	}
26	
27	/**
28	 * Serializes for legacy callers that still need a single string blob (tests, exports).
29	 * The live persistence path no longer writes this to the DB.
30	 */
31	export function serializeWorkerOutputEntries(
32	  outputEntries: AgentRecord["outputEntries"],
33	) {
34	  if (!Array.isArray(outputEntries) || outputEntries.length === 0) {
35	    return "";
36	  }
37	  try {
38	    return JSON.stringify(outputEntries);
39	  } catch {
40	    return "";
41	  }
42	}
43	
44	async function seedInitialDirectUserPrompt(worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect) {
45	  const initialPrompt = worker.initialPrompt.trim();
46	  if (!initialPrompt) {
47	    return;
48	  }
49	
50	  const run = await db.select({ mode: runs.mode }).from(runs).where(eq(runs.id, worker.runId)).get();
51	  if (run?.mode !== "direct" && run?.mode !== "commit") {
52	    return;
53	  }
54	
55	  const userMessages = await db
56	    .select()
57	    .from(messages)
58	    .where(eq(messages.runId, worker.runId))
59	    .orderBy(asc(messages.createdAt), asc(messages.id));
60	  const initialMessage = userMessages.find((message) => (
61	    message.role === "user"
62	    && message.content.trim() === initialPrompt
63	  ));
64	  if (!initialMessage) {
65	    return;
66	  }
67	
68	  const attachments = parseChatAttachmentsJson(initialMessage.attachmentsJson);
69	  await appendUserInputOnDelivery({
70	    id: initialMessage.id,
71	    runId: worker.runId,
72	    workerId: worker.id,
73	    text: initialMessage.content,
74	    deliveredAt: initialMessage.createdAt,
75	    attachments: attachments.map((attachment) => ({
76	      id: attachment.id,
77	      filename: attachment.name,
78	      mimeType: attachment.mimeType,
79	      sizeBytes: attachment.size,
80	    })),
81	  });
82	}
83	
84	export async function persistWorkerSnapshot(
85	  workerId: string,
86	  snapshot: PersistableWorkerSnapshot,
87	) {
88	  const worker = await db.select().from(workers).where(eq(workers.id, workerId)).get();
89	  if (!worker) {
90	    return;
91	  }
92	
93	  if (Array.isArray(snapshot.outputEntries) && snapshot.outputEntries.length > 0) {
94	    await seedInitialDirectUserPrompt(worker);
95	    await writeWorkerOutputEntries(worker.runId, workerId, snapshot.outputEntries);
96	  }
97	  await appendWorkerSessionMetadata({
98	    runId: worker.runId,
99	    workerId,
100	    sessionId: snapshot.sessionId,
101	    sessionMode: snapshot.sessionMode,
102	    source: "snapshot",
103	  });
104	  await db.update(workers).set({
105	    currentText: snapshot.currentText,
106	    lastText: snapshot.lastText || worker.lastText,
107	    updatedAt: new Date(),
108	  }).where(eq(workers.id, workerId));
109	}
110	
111	export { readWorkerOutputEntries };
112

1	/**
2	 * Compaction sweep for non-worker artifact streams.
3	 *
4	 * Run-level streams (execution_events / supervisor_interventions /
5	 * planning_review_findings) gzip to `<stream>.jsonl.gz` once the
6	 * owning run is in a terminal state AND the file hasn't been touched
7	 * for `minAgeMs`. The shared bytes layer in `append-only-store.ts`
8	 * already handles the chain+lock and atomic rename — this module just
9	 * picks candidates and calls into it.
10	 *
11	 * Worker streams keep their own sweep in `output-store.ts` until the
12	 * worker output-store relocation lands; the two will share this code
13	 * after that.
14	 */
15	import { promises as fs } from "node:fs";
16	import path from "node:path";
17	import { inArray } from "drizzle-orm";
18	import { db } from "@/server/db";
19	import { artifactStreams, runs } from "@/server/db/schema";
20	import {
21	  compactArtifactStream,
22	  resolveArtifactStreamLocation,
23	} from "./append-only-store";
24	import { recordStreamCompaction } from "./stream-metadata";
25	import { resolveArtifactRoot } from "./project-root";
26	import {
27	  normalizeArtifactOwnerId,
28	  type ArtifactStreamKind,
29	} from "./stream-types";
30	import { isTerminalRunStatus } from "@/lib/run-status";
31	import { emitNamedEvent } from "@/server/events/named-events";
32	
33	const DEFAULT_MIN_AGE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;
34	
35	export async function compactStaleArtifactStreams(options: {
36	  minAgeMs?: number;
37	  now?: number;
38	  kinds?: ArtifactStreamKind[];
39	} = {}): Promise<{
40	  compacted: Array<{ runId: string; kind: ArtifactStreamKind; ownerId: string }>;
41	  errors: Array<{ runId: string; kind: ArtifactStreamKind; error: string }>;
42	}> {
43	  const minAgeMs = options.minAgeMs ?? DEFAULT_MIN_AGE_MS;
44	  const now = options.now ?? Date.now();
45	  const kinds: ArtifactStreamKind[] = options.kinds ?? [
46	    "execution_events",
47	    "supervisor_interventions",
48	    "planning_review_findings",
49	  ];
50	
51	  const candidates = await db
52	    .select()
53	    .from(artifactStreams)
54	    .where(inArray(artifactStreams.kind, kinds));
55	  if (candidates.length === 0) return { compacted: [], errors: [] };
56	
57	  const runIds: string[] = Array.from(new Set(candidates.map((c) => c.runId)));
58	  if (runIds.length === 0) return { compacted: [], errors: [] };
59	  const runRows = await db
60	    .select({ id: runs.id, status: runs.status, projectPath: runs.projectPath })
61	    .from(runs)
62	    .where(inArray(runs.id, runIds));
63	  type RunRow = { id: string; status: string; projectPath: string | null };
64	  const runById = new Map<string, RunRow>(runRows.map((r) => [r.id, r as RunRow] as const));
65	
66	  const compacted: Array<{ runId: string; kind: ArtifactStreamKind; ownerId: string }> = [];
67	  const errors: Array<{ runId: string; kind: ArtifactStreamKind; error: string }> = [];
68	
69	  for (const row of candidates) {
70	    const run = runById.get(row.runId);
71	    if (!run) continue;
72	    if (!isTerminalRunStatus(run.status)) continue;
73	    try {
74	      // Stat the plaintext to make sure it exists and is old enough.
75	      const root = await resolveArtifactRoot({ runId: row.runId, projectPath: run.projectPath ?? null }, "read");
76	      const filePath = path.join(root.absolutePath, row.relativePath);
77	      let stat;
78	      try {
79	        stat = await fs.stat(filePath);
80	      } catch (error) {
81	        if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") continue;
82	        throw error;
83	      }
84	      if (now - stat.mtimeMs < minAgeMs) continue;
85	
86	      const location = await resolveArtifactStreamLocation(
87	        {
88	          runId: row.runId,
89	          kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
90	          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
91	          projectPath: run.projectPath ?? null,
92	        },
93	        "read",
94	      );
95	      const ok = await compactArtifactStream(location);
96	      await recordStreamCompaction(
97	        {
98	          runId: row.runId,
99	          kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
100	          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
101	        },
102	        ok,
103	        ok ? undefined : "compactArtifactStream returned false",
104	      );
105	      if (ok) {
106	        compacted.push({
107	          runId: row.runId,
108	          kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
109	          ownerId: normalizeArtifactOwnerId(row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId),
110	        });
111	        emitNamedEvent({
112	          kind: "artifact.compaction_completed",
113	          runId: row.runId,
114	          streamKind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
115	          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
116	        });
117	      } else {
118	        emitNamedEvent({
119	          kind: "artifact.compaction_failed",
120	          runId: row.runId,
121	          streamKind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
122	          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
123	          reason: "compactArtifactStream returned false",
124	        });
125	      }
126	    } catch (error) {
127	      const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
128	      errors.push({ runId: row.runId, kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind, error: message });
129	      await recordStreamCompaction(
130	        {
131	          runId: row.runId,
132	          kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
133	          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
134	        },
135	        false,
136	        message,
137	      );
138	      emitNamedEvent({
139	        kind: "artifact.compaction_failed",
140	        runId: row.runId,
141	        streamKind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
142	        ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
143	        reason: message,
144	      });
145	    }
146	  }
147	  return { compacted, errors };
148	}

async function compactArtifactStreamInternal(location: ArtifactStreamLocation): Promise<boolean> {
  let body: Buffer;
  try {
    body = await fs.readFile(location.filePath);
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return false;
    throw error;
  }
  tmpCounter = (tmpCounter + 1) >>> 0;
  const tmp = `${location.compressedFilePath}.tmp-${process.pid}-${Date.now()}-${tmpCounter}`;
  const compressed = gzipSync(body);
  try {
    await fs.writeFile(tmp, compressed);
    await fs.rename(tmp, location.compressedFilePath);
  } catch (error) {
    fs.unlink(tmp).catch(() => undefined);
    throw error;
  }
  await fs.unlink(location.filePath).catch(() => undefined);
  // Index offsets are into the plaintext file that no longer exists.
  await deleteIndex(location);
  return true;
}

/** Public compact entry point — acquires chain + lock. */
export async function compactArtifactStream(location: ArtifactStreamLocation): Promise<boolean> {
  return runOnArtifactChain(location.id, () => {
    if (!existsSync(location.filePath)) return Promise.resolve(false);
    return withArtifactFileLock(location, () => compactArtifactStreamInternal(location));
  });
}

/** Public expand entry point — acquires chain + lock. */
export async function expandArtifactStream(location: ArtifactStreamLocation): Promise<boolean> {
  return runOnArtifactChain(location.id, () =>
    withArtifactFileLock(location, () => expandArtifactStreamInternal(location)),
  );
}

// --- Delete --------------------------------------------------------

export async function deleteArtifactStreamFiles(location: ArtifactStreamLocation): Promise<void> {
  await runOnArtifactChain(location.id, () =>
    withArtifactFileLock(location, async () => {
      for (const target of [location.filePath, location.compressedFilePath]) {
        try {
          await fs.unlink(target);
        } catch (error) {
          if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") throw error;
        }
      }
      await deleteIndex(location);
    }),
  );
}

// --- Index-aware tail-N read ---------------------------------------

/**
 * Read the last `limit` entries from the plaintext stream using the
 * sparse index when available. Falls back to `null` when the boundary
 * can't be proven from a fast seek (no index, stale index, legacy
 * pre-seq lines in the indexed region, gzipped-only stream).
 *
 * Callers can fall back to the slower backward chunk scan in that case.
 */
export async function readEntriesTailWithIndex<T>(
  location: ArtifactStreamLocation,
  latestSeq: number,
  limit: number,

/**
 * Per-worker gzip sweep. Compacts any plaintext `.jsonl` whose worker is in a
 * terminal status and whose file hasn't been touched for at least
 * `minAgeMs`. Idempotent — safe to call repeatedly.
 *
 * Acquires the per-worker write chain before touching each file. An
 * earlier version of this sweep mutated files outside the chain, which
 * could drop an append racing the rename; that latent loss bug is fixed
 * here.
 */
export async function compactStaleWorkerOutputs(options: {
  minAgeMs?: number;
  now?: number;
} = {}): Promise<{ compacted: Array<{ runId: string; workerId: string }> }> {
  const minAgeMs = options.minAgeMs ?? WORKER_COMPACTION_MIN_AGE_MS;
  const now = options.now ?? Date.now();
  const root = runDataDir();
  let runDirs: string[];
  try {
    runDirs = await fs.readdir(root);
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
      return { compacted: [] };
    }
    throw error;
  }

  const { db } = await import("@/server/db");
  const { workers } = await import("@/server/db/schema");
  const { inArray } = await import("drizzle-orm");

  // Collect candidate (runId, workerId) pairs from disk before hitting the DB.
  const candidates: Array<{ runId: string; workerId: string; filePath: string }> = [];
  for (const entry of runDirs) {
    const runPath = path.join(root, entry);
    let stat;
    try {
      stat = await fs.stat(runPath);
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
    if (!stat.isDirectory()) continue;
    // Legacy transcripts sit directly in the run directory; once a run has an
    // `artifact_streams` row they are written to a `workers/` subdirectory
    // instead. Scanning only the flat layout meant no modern transcript was
    // ever swept, so run-data grew without bound.
    for (const dir of [runPath, path.join(runPath, WORKER_STREAM_DIR_NAME)]) {
      let workerFiles: string[];
      try {
        workerFiles = await fs.readdir(dir);
      } catch {
        continue;
      }
      for (const file of workerFiles) {
        if (!file.endsWith(".jsonl")) continue;
        const filePath = path.join(dir, file);
        let fileStat;
        try {
          fileStat = await fs.stat(filePath);
        } catch {
          continue;
        }
        if (!fileStat.isFile()) continue;
        if (now - fileStat.mtimeMs < minAgeMs) continue;
        candidates.push({
          runId: entry,
          workerId: file.slice(0, -".jsonl".length),
          filePath,
        });
      }
    }
  }

async function expandWorkerOutputFileInternal(paths: WorkerStreamPaths): Promise<boolean> {
  const source = paths.compressedFilePath;
  let body: Buffer;
  try {
    body = await fs.readFile(source);
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
      return false;
    }
    throw error;
  }
  const decompressed = gunzipSync(body);
  const target = paths.filePath;
  tmpCounter = (tmpCounter + 1) >>> 0;
  const tmp = `${target}.tmp-${process.pid}-${Date.now()}-${tmpCounter}`;
  try {
    await fs.writeFile(tmp, decompressed);
    await fs.rename(tmp, target);
  } catch (error) {
    fs.unlink(tmp).catch(() => undefined);
    throw error;
  }
  await fs.unlink(source).catch(() => undefined);
  // Caches stay valid: the bytes are the same, only the file shape changed.
  return true;
}

export async function compactWorkerOutputFile(runId: string, workerId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return runOnChain(runId, workerId, async () => {
    const paths = await workerStreamPaths(runId, workerId, "read");
    if (!existsSync(paths.filePath)) {
      return false;
    }
    return withWorkerFileLock(runId, workerId, (lockedPaths) => compactWorkerOutputFileInternal(lockedPaths));
  });
}

export async function expandWorkerOutputFile(runId: string, workerId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return runOnChain(runId, workerId, () =>
    withWorkerFileLock(runId, workerId, (paths) => expandWorkerOutputFileInternal(paths)));
}

Confirmed: the missing head content is fully present in the raw archive. The head data is recoverable. Here is my analysis.

## Summary

The missing heads are **not** caused by truncation, compaction, or retention. They are caused by **lazy file creation combined with a seq cursor that is seeded from the DB rather than the file** — the file was created part-way through the conversation and only ever appended forward from that moment.

### 1. How entries get appended and how `latest_seq` is maintained

Two writers, both in `src/server/workers/output-store.ts`:

- `appendWorkerEntryWithResult` (:828) — single entry
- `writeWorkerOutputEntries` (:928) — batch, called by `persistWorkerSnapshot` (`src/server/workers/snapshots.ts:95`)

Both take the per-worker chain + on-disk lock (`withWorkerFileLock`, :667), then open the target with flag `"a"` and `appendFile` (:875-881, :1011-1017). **Every write is strictly `O_APPEND`. There is no code path anywhere in this module that opens the worker jsonl for truncate/rewrite.** The only file-replacing operations are compact/expand (gzip round-trip, :540-591 of `append-only-store.ts`), which are content-preserving, and `deleteArtifactStreamFiles` (:610), which removes the file entirely.

`latest_seq` is maintained by `commitArtifactAppend` (:899-904, :1022-1028) after each successful append, recording the seq of the last written entry.

### 2. The causal mechanism — `refreshChainCaches` at output-store.ts:697-774

This is the bug. On first write to a chain the seq cursor is computed as:

```ts
const nextSeq = Math.max(rawMaxSeq, dbLatestSeq) + 1;   // :767
```

where `rawMaxSeq` comes from the file (0 if the file does not exist) and `dbLatestSeq` comes from `artifact_streams.latest_seq` (:754-766). The comment at :727-732 explains this `max()` was deliberately added as "cross-process safety" so the writer never reuses a seq another process claimed.

The consequence: **if the file is absent/empty but the DB row carries a high `latest_seq`, the writer starts numbering at `dbLatestSeq + 1` and appends only from that point forward. It never backfills the entries for seqs `1..dbLatestSeq`.** The resulting file's first record has `seq = dbLatestSeq + 1` with `latest_seq` far above it, and — critically — no supersede columns are set, because supersede is not involved at all. (The schema has no `superseded_from_seq` / `superseded_seq_ranges` columns; `sqlite3 .schema artifact_streams` shows only `latest_seq`, `latest_record_id`, `status`, `compacted_at`. Those fields could never have been set.)

### 3. Does the writer backfill pre-existing in-memory entries? No — and it structurally cannot

`persistWorkerSnapshot` (`snapshots.ts:93-96`) passes `snapshot.outputEntries`, which is the agent runtime's **live window**, hard-capped at 80 entries by `pruneLiveEntries` (`src/server/agent-runtime/output-store.ts:266-276`, `LIVE_OUTPUT_ENTRY_LIMIT = 80` at :8). Older entries are `splice`d out of memory and exist only in the raw archive. So even a full snapshot flush can only ever contribute the most recent ~80 records. `writeWorkerOutputEntries` additionally drops the synthetic `output-archive-marker` (:951-955).

So: **append-from-now-forward only, with at most an 80-entry lookback. No backfill.**

### 4. Why these three runs and not the other ten

The evidence on disk matches exactly:

- All 10 intact run-data dirs have mtime `Aug 3 19:33` and files starting at seq 1 — written in one batch by a backfill/migration pass at 17:33 UTC.
- The 3 damaged runs have **later** file mtimes (`19:35`, `19:37`, and dir `19:42`) — these were the runs still **live** when the migration ran.

The first surviving record of `e51514929b72` is timestamped `2026-08-03T17:31:55.812Z` at `seq 1399` — i.e. the file's first byte was written at roughly the migration moment, not at conversation start. The three live runs raced the batch: their `artifact_streams.latest_seq` was already high (1398 / 267 / 772) while their project-local file did not yet exist, so `refreshChainCaches` seeded `nextSeq` from `dbLatestSeq` and the newly-created file began mid-stream.

Corroborating: **all three files have zero internal seq gaps** (contiguous 1399→1756, 268→738, 773→967). A truncation or head-dropping rewrite would be unlikely to leave a perfectly contiguous tail; a fresh file appended forward from a seeded cursor produces exactly this.

Also note `workers.output_entries_json = '[]'` for all workers is consistent with `scripts/migrate-output-entries-to-disk.ts:31` having cleared the column after migrating.

A secondary contributor worth flagging: `workerStreamPaths` (:98-172) caches the resolved path, and read-mode resolution does **not** create the `artifact_streams` row (:140-141). The `ensuredForWriteByKey` set (:96) exists specifically to patch a prior incarnation of this same class of bug — the comment at :86-95 documents hand-repairs being needed "every time a worker is spawned after a cancel."

### 5. Uncommitted diff

`git diff --stat -- src/server/artifacts src/server/workers scripts/ src/server/agent-runtime` returns **empty**. Nothing in the working tree touches this behavior; the damage predates and is independent of the uncommitted changes.

### 6. Recoverability — the head data IS recoverable

The pre-cutover raw archive survives at `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/.omniharness/agent-runtime-output/<runId>-worker-1.jsonl` (cwd-relative, per `openAgentOutputArchive` at `src/server/agent-runtime/output-store.ts:257-264`). I verified all three:

| run | archive bridge entries | live file entries | missing entries present in archive |
|---|---|---|---|
| e51514929b72 | 1615 | 283 | 1412 |
| e74cf7a81b7f | 751 | 235 | 583 |
| ef23fac96fdb | 986 | 140 | 891 |

Archive heads start at `16:58:55`, `17:00:28`, `16:49:25` — the true conversation starts, well before the surviving file heads. For the first two, the live file's first entry id is found at archive positions 1267 and 129 respectively, confirming clean prefix alignment.

`scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts` is purpose-built to replay these and is idempotent (dedups by `entry.id`, :146). **Caveat:** replayed entries would be assigned *new* seqs starting above the current `latest_seq`, so the recovered head would land after the tail in seq order rather than before it. Restoring correct chronological ordering needs either a seq-renumbering repair (see `scripts/artifact-repair.ts`) or ordering the UI by `timestamp`.

**Two urgent preservation warnings:**
1. `openAgentOutputArchive` passes `{ truncate: !input.resume }` (:262) — **the archive is truncated on a non-resume start of the same worker.** If any of these three conversations is restarted without resume, the recovery source is destroyed.
2. `cleanupRunArtifacts` (`src/server/artifacts/cleanup.ts:88-107`) deletes `<runId>-*.jsonl` from that same directory on conversation delete.

I recommend copying those three archive files somewhere safe before doing anything else. I have not modified any files.

async function withWorkerFileLock<T>(
  runId: string,
  workerId: string,
  task: (paths: WorkerStreamPaths) => Promise<T>,
): Promise<T> {
  const paths = await workerStreamPaths(runId, workerId, "write");
  await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(paths.filePath), { recursive: true });
  // Appending an empty string with `a` is an atomic touch.
  await fs.writeFile(paths.filePath, "", { flag: "a" });
  const release = await acquireWorkerFileLock(paths.lockPath);
  try {
    return await task(paths);
  } finally {
    await release();
  }
}

async function readWorkerFileState(runId: string, workerId: string) {
  const paths = await workerStreamPaths(runId, workerId, "read");
  try {
    const stat = await fs.stat(paths.filePath);
    return { size: stat.size, mtimeMs: stat.mtimeMs };
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
      return { size: 0, mtimeMs: 0 };
    }
    throw error;
  }
}

Conclusive. The surviving sequences are perfectly contiguous — so this was a clean front-truncation (file replaced starting mid-stream), not scattered corruption.

## Findings

### Timestamp convention (resolved)
- **`remote-restart.log` = LOCAL time (UTC+2).** Proven by a self-dating line: prefix `[2026-08-03 19:44:13]` wraps an HTTP header `date: 'Mon, 03 Aug 2026 17:44:13 GMT'` — exactly +2h.
- **`memory-trace.jsonl` = UTC** (explicit `Z`: `"ts":"2026-08-03T17:47:53.969Z"`).
- Filesystem `ls -T` times are local. So the 19:33:42 mtimes = **17:33:42 UTC**.

### What actually happened at 17:33:42 UTC — not a restart, migration, or backfill

The directories were **not created**. They already existed; what changed at 17:33:42 was that every run's `execution-events.jsonl` was **gzipped in place to `.jsonl.gz`** — a compaction sweep. The rename+unlink bumps each parent directory's mtime simultaneously, which is what made them look "created at once."

The mechanism is the 15-second watchdog tick, not a boot event:
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/supervisor/runtime-watchdog.ts:13` — `const WATCHDOG_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000;`
- Lines 61-66 fire both sweeps every tick, fire-and-forget: `void compactStaleWorkerOutputs()` and `void compactStaleArtifactStreams()`.
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/artifacts/compaction.ts:33` — `DEFAULT_MIN_AGE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000`, and line 72 gates on `isTerminalRunStatus`.

So the trigger was simply: **runs crossed into terminal status + 5 minutes idle, and the next watchdog tick swept them all together.** Corroborating: `c300559b69d9` kept its Aug 1 mtime because it was already compacted earlier — exactly the idempotent behavior expected.

### 1. Restarts in the window
No app-server restart at 17:33:42. `remote-restart.log` has a **total gap from 19:24:59 to 19:40:22 local** — nothing logged when the compaction ran. The `memory-trace` "boot" bursts (pids 49722, 52920, 55785, 57711, 75422) are **test-suite runs**, not the server: they spawn into temp dirs like `omni-lifecycle-sub-XtevsA`, `codex-credentials-project-ZF6hq4`. The real server is pid 45731 (`remote-restart.pid.json`, `startedAt: 1785761270924` = 12:47 UTC), which ran continuously across the whole window.

### 2. Migration/backfill lines
**None.** Every `gzip` hit in the 125MB log is an HTTP `content-encoding` response header. The compaction path emits `emitNamedEvent(...)` only — it writes nothing to stdout/stderr, so the sweep is **completely silent on disk**. That silence is itself the finding: the compaction has no operational logging.

### 3-4. Run e51514929b72 and the 17:37:27 idle
No errors for it in either log — it appears **zero times** in `remote-restart.log`. Its final execution event is `seq 6, 2026-08-03T17:37:27.268Z`, matching the worker dir mtime 19:37:27 exactly. Its worker file's last entry is `17:37:27.265Z`. So it went terminal cleanly, then its `execution-events` was compacted at 19:42:40 local (~5 min later, per `minAgeMs`) — textbook, no error.

### The three runs: real data loss, distinct from all others

This is the significant finding. All three are **front-truncated**:

| run | first entry type | first seq | window |
|---|---|---|---|
| e51514929b72 | `tool_call` | **1399** | 17:31:55 → 17:37:27 |
| e74cf7a81b7f | `tool_call_update` | **268** | 17:02:10 → 17:35:49 |
| ef23fac96fdb | `usage` | **773** | 17:04:02 → 17:07:41 |
| *healthy* (1c9615243d3a, 73fe3ee52059, 565be7df7d27, c300559b69d9) | `user_input` | **1** | full |

Every healthy run starts at `seq=1` with `user_input`. These three start mid-stream at seq 1399/268/773 — and their surviving seqs are **perfectly contiguous with zero gaps**. That rules out scattered corruption: the file was cleanly replaced with only a recent tail.

The shared trait is that all three were **actively running during the sweep window** (unlike the quiescent older runs), and all three are the songclipper runs whose first execution event is `"Conversation title generation failed... API key not valid"`.

**Likely mechanism** — a compact/expand race in `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/workers/output-store.ts:667`:

```js
async function withWorkerFileLock(runId, workerId, task) {
  const paths = await workerStreamPaths(runId, workerId, "write");
  await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(paths.filePath), { recursive: true });
  // Appending an empty string with `a` is an atomic touch.
  await fs.writeFile(paths.filePath, "", { flag: "a" });
  const release = await acquireWorkerFileLock(paths.lockPath);  // <-- lock AFTER touch
```

The empty-placeholder touch happens **before** the lock is acquired. The code itself acknowledges this hazard at line 837: *"If a compaction race somehow stranded the plaintext file under .gz, expand it first so cache refresh sees the live transcript rather than the lock-created empty placeholder."* If a writer creates the placeholder while the sweep is mid-compact (gzip written, plaintext not yet unlinked), the sweep's `fs.unlink(source)` removes the real data, `readAllPersistedEntries` then sees a non-empty-but-partial plaintext and returns early (line ~785) without consulting the `.gz`, and subsequent appends continue from the DB-backed `latestSeq` — producing exactly the observed contiguous-tail-starting-at-a-high-seq signature. The seq counter survived because it is recovered from `artifactStreams.latestSeq` (line ~767), not from the file.

Supporting artifact: `e74cf7a81b7f/workers` has an mtime of **19:49:17**, later than its file's 19:35:49 and after the sweep — consistent with lock/placeholder churn in that directory. That run also holds the only remaining uncompacted `execution-events.jsonl` plus a **0-byte `execution-events.jsonl.idx`** (19:34:29), i.e. an index invalidated mid-operation.

### Bottom line
The 17:33 mass-timestamp event was a **routine, silent gzip compaction sweep** by the supervisor watchdog (15s tick, 5-min idle threshold on terminal runs) — not a restart, migration, backfill, or new code. It is benign for the 10 runs that were idle. But for the three runs that were *live* during the sweep, it coincided with genuine loss of early transcript history, and the placeholder-before-lock ordering in `withWorkerFileLock` is the most probable culprit. I modified no files.

1	/**
2	 * Superseded worker-stream ranges.
3	 *
4	 * "Retry from here" and "edit in place" rewind a conversation to an earlier
5	 * message: the messages after it are deleted and the message is re-delivered,
6	 * either to a fresh worker or to the same worker on a resumed ACP session. The
7	 * worker stream is append-only, so everything the abandoned attempt produced —
8	 * including the original copy of the re-delivered user message — stays on disk
9	 * and used to keep rendering. The transcript then showed the same user message
10	 * twice (once at its old position, above output it had already been rewound
11	 * past) and interleaved the discarded answers with the new ones.
12	 *
13	 * Recovery records the discarded seq range on the worker instead, and readers
14	 * skip those entries. Nothing is deleted; the raw stream stays intact.
15	 */
16	
17	export type SupersededSeqRange = {
18	  /** First superseded seq, inclusive — the original delivery of the message. */
19	  from: number;
20	  /** Last superseded seq, inclusive — the stream tip when the rewind happened. */
21	  through: number;
22	};
23	
24	function isUsableRange(range: SupersededSeqRange) {
25	  return Number.isFinite(range.from)
26	    && Number.isFinite(range.through)
27	    && range.from >= 1
28	    && range.through >= range.from;
29	}
30	
31	export function parseSupersededSeqRanges(value: string | null | undefined): SupersededSeqRange[] {
32	  if (!value?.trim()) {
33	    return [];
34	  }
35	  let parsed: unknown;
36	  try {
37	    parsed = JSON.parse(value);
38	  } catch {
39	    return [];
40	  }
41	  if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) {
42	    return [];
43	  }
44	  const ranges = parsed.flatMap((entry) => {
45	    if (typeof entry !== "object" || entry === null) {
46	      return [];
47	    }
48	    const record = entry as { from?: unknown; through?: unknown };
49	    const range = {
50	      from: Math.floor(Number(record.from)),
51	      through: Math.floor(Number(record.through)),
52	    };
53	    return isUsableRange(range) ? [range] : [];
54	  });
55	  return mergeSupersededSeqRanges(ranges);
56	}
57	
58	/** Sort and coalesce overlapping/adjacent ranges so the stored list stays small. */
59	export function mergeSupersededSeqRanges(ranges: SupersededSeqRange[]): SupersededSeqRange[] {
60	  const usable = ranges.filter(isUsableRange).sort((left, right) => left.from - right.from);
61	  const merged: SupersededSeqRange[] = [];
62	  for (const range of usable) {
63	    const previous = merged.at(-1);
64	    if (previous && range.from <= previous.through + 1) {
65	      previous.through = Math.max(previous.through, range.through);
66	      continue;
67	    }
68	    merged.push({ ...range });
69	  }
70	  return merged;
71	}
72	
73	export function serializeSupersededSeqRanges(ranges: SupersededSeqRange[]): string | null {
74	  const merged = mergeSupersededSeqRanges(ranges);
75	  return merged.length > 0 ? JSON.stringify(merged) : null;
76	}
77	
78	export function isSupersededSeq(seq: number | null | undefined, ranges: SupersededSeqRange[]) {
79	  if (typeof seq !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(seq)) {
80	    return false;
81	  }
82	  return ranges.some((range) => seq >= range.from && seq <= range.through);
83	}
84	
85	/** Drop the entries that belong to a discarded branch. */
86	export function withoutSupersededEntries<T extends { seq?: number | null }>(
87	  entries: T[],
88	  ranges: SupersededSeqRange[],
89	): T[] {
90	  return ranges.length === 0 ? entries : entries.filter((entry) => !isSupersededSeq(entry.seq, ranges));
91	}
92

## Claude subagent agent-a6b8fd7b7592c0a98: Claude · 2026-08-03T17:51:45.340Z

```text
I have a complete picture. Here are my findings.

## Summary

The transcript is fetched **tail-first, then merged forward** — but there is exactly one path that **replaces** the whole list, and it is reachable at runtime. The truncated artifact does *not* need a replace to hurt you, though: the truncation is invisible in steady state and only manifests on a cold load or a run-switch.

### 1. How the client fetches entries

Two independent stores feed the conversation, merged in the UI:

- **`ConversationTranscriptManager`** (`/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/ConversationTranscriptManager.ts`) — run-scoped, hits `GET /api/conversations/:runId/transcript`. Cold start = `fetchTail` with `limit=100`; steady state = `fetchForward` with an opaque `afterToken` (per-worker seq cursors); scroll-back = `fetchOlder` with `beforeToken`.
- **`WorkerEntriesManager`** (`/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/WorkerEntriesManager.ts`) — worker-scoped, hits `GET /api/workers/:workerId/entries`. Cold start = `fetchTail(limit=100)`; steady state = `fetchForward(afterSeq=latestContiguousSeq)`; scroll-back = `fetchBefore`.

Both are combined in `selectDirectConversationEntries` (`/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/direct-worker-stream-loading.ts:70-96`), and the result is fed to `Terminal` via `conversationEntries` (`ConversationMain.tsx:911-924`).

Merge semantics differ per path:

- `ConversationTranscriptManager.ts:185` — `fetchForward` **merges**: `coalesceWorkerEntriesById([...current.entries, ...response.entries])`.
- `ConversationTranscriptManager.ts:216` — `fetchOlder` **merges** (prepends).
- **`ConversationTranscriptManager.ts:154` — `fetchTail` REPLACES**: `entries: coalesceWorkerEntriesById(response.entries)`, discarding `current.entries` entirely.

`WorkerEntriesManager` behaves the same way: `applyFetchResult` (line 641-666) merges by appending only entries at `nextContiguous + 1`, but `fetchTail` (line 498-508) does `entries: sorted` — a hard replace of the window.

### 2. What the truncated file produces

For the transcript endpoint, `readWorkerEntriesTail` (`/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/workers/output-store.ts:1312`) scans the tail of the JSONL. With only 1399..1756 on disk it returns the last 100 (1657..1756) and computes `hasOlder` from the byte scan, so `hasOlder` stays true — the "load more" affordance is still offered (`ConversationMain.tsx:1141-1158`).

The trap is `readWorkerEntriesBefore` (`output-store.ts:1513-1536`): it does a full canonical read and filters `entry.seq < beforeSeq`. Once the client scrolls back to seq 1399, `older` is empty, `slice` is empty, `lowestKeptSeq` is `undefined`, so `hasOlder` computes as **`false`** and the response is `{entries: []}`. Because `fetchOlder` merges rather than replaces, nothing vanishes — the user just hits a wall at seq 1399 and the "load more" control disappears. **Everything before seq 1399 is silently unreachable, presented as if the conversation simply began there.** There is no error, no gap marker, no indication that ~1398 records were lost.

Notably `readWorkerEntriesBefore` returns `hasOlder: false` *and* `latestSeq: 0` when `beforeSeq <= 1` (line 1519-1520), but in the truncation case it takes the normal path and still reports the honest-looking `hasOlder: false`. The UI has no way to distinguish "you reached the beginning" from "the beginning is gone".

### 3. Does sending a message replace the transcript?

**No — not directly, and this is the important negative finding.** I traced every trigger:

- `useConversationTranscript` calls `ensureLoaded` on `[runId, enabled]` only (`ConversationTranscriptManager.ts:270-273`), and `ensureLoaded` early-returns when status is `loaded` or `loading` (line 103-109). So a re-render after send does not re-tail.
- The polling effect calls `refresh` (line 279), which routes to `fetchForward` whenever `latestToken` exists (line 116) — the merge path.
- `refreshIntervalMs` flips from 5000 to 2000 when `showDirectControlWorkingIndicator` goes true on send (`resolveDirectWorkerStreamRefreshInterval`, `direct-worker-stream-loading.ts:98-113`). That tears down and recreates the interval, but the callback is still `refresh` → `fetchForward`. No replace.
- SSE wake-ups go through `onWakeUp`/`onKnownSeqs`/`onStreamResync` (`WorkerEntriesManager.ts:405-464`), all of which call `fetchForward` — merge only.

The one way to reach the replacing `fetchTail` post-send is **`runId` changing** (new run) or the manager's state being absent/`error`. Sending a message into an existing run does not do that. So "I sent a message and everything changed immediately" is **not** explained by a send-triggered refetch-and-replace of the transcript.

The far more likely explanation, given the established facts, is the **worker id changing** — a cancel→respawn or a retry/edit rewind. `useWorkerStream` is keyed on `primaryConversationWorkerId` (`ConversationMain.tsx:853-854`, hook at `WorkerEntriesManager.ts:867-881`); a new worker id means a brand-new `WorkerStreamState` and a cold `fetchTail` against a worker whose file is truncated. Combined with `isUsingConversationTranscriptEntries` (`ConversationMain.tsx:934`) flipping the render source between the transcript and the direct stream, the visible list can change wholesale in one frame.

### 4. Does the uncommitted diff introduce or fix this?

**Neither — the diff is orthogonal, but one hunk makes truncation harder to notice and one is a latent correctness risk.**

The working-tree changes are performance and flicker work:

- `EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager.ts` and `WorkerEntriesManager.ts`: localStorage writes coalesced onto a 1s trailing timer with an in-memory envelope serving reads, plus `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` flush handlers. Does not touch fetch or merge semantics.
- `WorkerEntriesManager.ts:666`: `entries: merged.length > previous.entries.length ? merged : previous.entries` — an identity-preservation optimization. This *strengthens* merge-over-replace: a forward fetch that returns nothing now provably cannot change `entries` identity.
- `EventStreamStateManager.ts:175-221` (`mergeDegradedAgentHumanInput`): preserves `pendingPermissions`/`pendingElicitations` across `bridgeMissing` frames. Flicker fix, unrelated.
- `events.ts:954-984`: `hasDeliveredRuntimePayload` latch stops regressing to the degraded persisted payload. Flicker fix, unrelated.
- `events.ts:162-172`: queued-message status filter narrowed from `["pending","delivering"]` to `"pending"`. Unrelated to entries.

Two observations worth flagging:

**`ConversationMain.tsx:901-905` is a latent bug risk.** `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` round-trips `supersededSeqRanges` through a `useMemo` keyed on the serialized string. That is correct for the stated purpose, but it means `supersededSeqRanges` is now a *stable* reference that `selectDirectConversationEntries` filters against (`direct-worker-stream-loading.ts:83-86`). If a rewind writes a range covering the surviving 1399..1756 window, the memo will correctly recompute — but combined with the truncation, entries filtered as superseded plus entries missing from disk are indistinguishable to the user. Both just disappear.

**The coalescing flush makes the localStorage cache staler.** `WorkerEntriesManager.getCachedEntries` (line 700-714) hydrates from localStorage on cold start, trimmed to the last 100. With the diff, that cache can now lag up to 1s behind. This does not cause data loss (the cache is a preview and `needsTailValidation` forces a server tail fetch — line 300, 374-376), but it does mean the first paint after a reload is more likely to show cached entries that the truncated server file can no longer confirm.

### Bottom line on user-visible effect

With seq 1..1398 gone from `<workerId>.jsonl` and `output_entries_json` empty, the user sees a conversation that **appears to start at seq 1399**. In steady state nothing vanishes mid-session, because every live path merges. The loss becomes visible on a page reload, a run switch, or a worker respawn — at which point the cold `fetchTail` replaces the window with the truncated tail. Scrolling back stops at 1399 and the "load more" control disappears (`readWorkerEntriesBefore` returns `hasOlder: false`), presenting silent truncation as a natural conversation start. The reported "everything changed immediately" is most consistent with a worker-id change (respawn/rewind) forcing a cold tail load, not with the send itself.

Cold start = `fetchTail(limit=100)`; steady state = `fetchForward(afterSeq=latestContiguousSeq)`; scroll-back = `fetchBefore`.\n\nBoth are combined in `selectDirectConversationEntries` (`/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/direct-worker-stream-loading.ts:70-96`), and the result is fed to `Terminal` via `conversationEntries` (`ConversationMain.tsx:911-924`).\n\nMerge semantics differ per path:\n\n- `ConversationTranscriptManager.ts:185` — `fetchForward` **merges**: `coalesceWorkerEntriesById([...current.entries, ...response.entries])`.\n- `ConversationTranscriptManager.ts:216` — `fetchOlder` **merges** (prepends).\n- **`ConversationTranscriptManager.ts:154` — `fetchTail` REPLACES**: `entries: coalesceWorkerEntriesById(response.entries)`, discarding `current.entries` entirely.\n\n`WorkerEntriesManager` behaves the same way: `applyFetchResult` (line 641-666) merges by appending only entries at `nextContiguous + 1`, but `fetchTail` (line 498-508) does `entries: sorted` — a hard replace of the window.\n\n### 2. What the truncated file produces\n\nFor the transcript endpoint, `readWorkerEntriesTail` (`/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/workers/output-store.ts:1312`) scans the tail of the JSONL. With only 1399..1756 on disk it returns the last 100 (1657..1756) and computes `hasOlder` from the byte scan, so `hasOlder` stays true — the \"load more\" affordance is still offered (`ConversationMain.tsx:1141-1158`).\n\nThe trap is `readWorkerEntriesBefore` (`output-store.ts:1513-1536`): it does a full canonical read and filters `entry.seq < beforeSeq`. Does sending a message replace the transcript?\n\n**No — not directly, and this is the important negative finding.** I traced every trigger:\n\n- `useConversationTranscript` calls `ensureLoaded` on `[runId, enabled]` only (`ConversationTranscriptManager.ts:270-273`), and `ensureLoaded` early-returns when status is `loaded` or `loading` (line 103-109). export function openAgentOutputArchive(input: { dataDir?: string | null; name: string; resume?: boolean }) {
  const dataDir = input.dataDir?.trim() || join(process.cwd(), ".omniharness");
  return new AgentOutputArchive(
    input.name,
    join(dataDir, "agent-runtime-output", `${sanitizePathPart(input.name)}.jsonl`),
    { truncate: !input.resume },
  );
}

function pruneLiveEntries(record: AgentRecord) {
  const totalEntries = record.outputArchive.stats().totalEntries;
  const liveLimit = totalEntries > LIVE_OUTPUT_ENTRY_LIMIT ? LIVE_OUTPUT_ENTRY_LIMIT - 1 : LIVE_OUTPUT_ENTRY_LIMIT;
  if (record.outputEntries.length <= liveLimit) {
    return;
  }
  record.outputEntries.splice(0, record.outputEntries.length - liveLimit);
  if (record.activeOutputEntryId && !record.outputEntries.some((entry) => entry.id === record.activeOutputEntryId)) {
    record.activeOutputEntryId = null;
  }
}

export function appendOutputEntry(record: AgentRecord, input: OutputEntryInput) {
  const archiveEntry = record.outputArchive.append(input);
  record.activeOutputEntryId = null;

## Claude · 2026-08-03T17:52:36.521Z

## What happened

Your conversation isn't lost — but ~80% of it did get detached from the UI. Here's the actual state.

**Run `e51514929b72`** — "Server side export", project `/Users/masterman/NLP/songclipper`, status `done`, worker idle since 19:37 local.

The UI reads agent output from `songclipper/.omniharness/run-data/e51514929b72/workers/e51514929b72-worker-1.jsonl`. That file contains **only seq 1399–1756** (358 entries, starting 19:31:55). Sequences **1–1398 are absent** — everything from the run's start at 18:58 up to 19:31.

This is not a supersede/rewind: `superseded_from_seq` and `superseded_seq_ranges` are both null. And there's no DB fallback — `workers.output_entries_json` is `'[]'` for every worker (a prior migration cleared it).

## Why it looked instant

The surviving seqs are perfectly contiguous, which rules out scattered corruption. What happened is that the writer **started a fresh file mid-stream**: `refreshChainCaches` seeds the seq cursor as `max(fileMaxSeq, dbLatestSeq) + 1` (`src/server/workers/output-store.ts:767`). With the file missing but `artifact_streams.latest_seq` already at 1398, it began numbering at 1399 and only appended forward. There is no backfill path — and even a full snapshot flush can only contribute ~80 entries, since the live in-memory window is hard-capped at `LIVE_OUTPUT_ENTRY_LIMIT = 80`.

What made the file go missing at that moment is the one part I could **not** nail down conclusively. The strongest candidate is a race with the watchdog's silent compaction sweep (`runtime-watchdog.ts:13`, 15s tick; `artifacts/compaction.ts`), against `withWorkerFileLock` creating its empty placeholder *before* acquiring the lock (`output-store.ts:667`) — the code already comments on exactly this hazard at line 837. Two of my three investigation threads landed on slightly different framings of the trigger, so treat the mechanism as probable, not proven.

One correction to your read: **sending the message didn't cause it.** Every live update path merges rather than replaces. The loss only becomes visible on a cold load — page reload, run switch, or worker respawn — where `fetchTail` replaces the window. Worse, when you scroll back, `readWorkerEntriesBefore` returns `hasOlder: false` at seq 1399, so the "load more" control just disappears and it renders as if the conversation naturally began there. No error, no gap marker. That silent presentation is why it felt like the conversation got lost.

**You're not the only run affected**: `e74cf7a81b7f` (lost 267) and `ef23fac96fdb` (lost 772) have the same signature. The other 10 runs are intact at seq 1..N.

## The good news, and one urgent risk

The full history survives in the raw archive:

```
.omniharness/agent-runtime-output/e51514929b72-worker-1.jsonl   2.2 MB, 1930 entries, from 18:58:55
```

All three damaged runs have complete archives, and `scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts` exists to replay them (idempotent, dedups by `entry.id`).

**The risk:** `openAgentOutputArchive` passes `{ truncate: !input.resume }` (`src/server/agent-runtime/output-store.ts:262`). If any of those three conversations is restarted *without* resume, the archive is wiped and the history is gone for good. `cleanupRunArtifacts` also deletes these on conversation delete.

I haven't changed anything. Two things I'd suggest, in order:

1. **Copy those three archive files somewhere outside `.omniharness/` now** — cheap insurance before anything else touches them.
2. Then decide on recovery. Note the replay assigns *new* seqs above the current `latest_seq`, so the recovered head would sort *after* the tail unless we either renumber (`scripts/artifact-repair.ts`) or order the UI by timestamp. Worth deciding deliberately rather than just running the backfill.

Want me to do the backup first, or dig further into pinning the compaction race?

=== BACKFILL ===
/**
 * Backfill the unified worker conversation stream from legacy
 * `.omniharness/agent-runtime-output/<workerId>.jsonl` files written
 * by the agent runtime's pre-cutover output archive.
 *
 * Sessions that ran before the worker conversation stream cutover never
 * had their bridge-produced entries (message / thought / tool_call /
 * tool_call_update / permission) routed through `appendWorkerEntry`.
 * The frontend now reads exclusively from the worker stream, so those
 * conversations appear empty in the UI even though the raw bridge
 * output is on disk.
 *
 * This script replays each runtime-output line through
 * `appendWorkerEntry`, which is idempotent (dedup by `entry.id`). Safe
 * to re-run.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts --dry-run
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts --workerId <id>
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts --verbose
 */
import fs from "fs";
import path from "path";
import readline from "readline";
import { db } from "@/server/db";
import { workers as workersTable } from "@/server/db/schema";
import { appendWorkerEntry } from "@/server/workers/output-store";
import type { BridgeWorkerEntryType, WorkerEntry } from "@/server/workers/entries-types";

const BRIDGE_TYPES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set<BridgeWorkerEntryType>([
  "message",
  "thought",
  "tool_call",
  "tool_call_update",
  "permission",
]);

interface Options {
  dryRun: boolean;
  workerId: string | null;
  verbose: boolean;
  runtimeOutputDir: string;
}

interface FileStats {
  workerId: string;
  runId: string | null;
  totalLines: number;
  appended: number;
  skippedDuplicate: number;
  skippedNonBridge: number;
  malformed: number;
}

function parseOptions(argv: string[]): Options {
  const opts: Options = {
    dryRun: false,
    workerId: null,
    verbose: false,
    runtimeOutputDir: path.resolve(process.cwd(), ".omniharness/agent-runtime-output"),
  };
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 1) {
    const arg = argv[i];
    if (arg === "--dry-run") opts.dryRun = true;
    else if (arg === "--verbose") opts.verbose = true;
    else if (arg === "--workerId") opts.workerId = argv[++i] ?? null;
    else if (arg === "--runtime-output-dir") opts.runtimeOutputDir = path.resolve(argv[++i] ?? "");
    else if (arg === "--help" || arg === "-h") {
      console.log("Usage: pnpm tsx scripts/backfill-runtime-output-to-worker-stream.ts [--dry-run] [--workerId <id>] [--verbose]");
      process.exit(0);
    }
  }
  return opts;
}

async function processFile(
  filePath: string,
  workerId: string,
  runId: string,
  opts: Options,
): Promise<FileStats> {
  const stats: FileStats = {
    workerId,
    runId,
    totalLines: 0,
    appended: 0,
    skippedDuplicate: 0,
    skippedNonBridge: 0,
    malformed: 0,
  };

  const rl = readline.createInterface({
    input: fs.createReadStream(filePath, { encoding: "utf8" }),
    crlfDelay: Infinity,
  });

  for await (const line of rl) {
    if (!line.trim()) continue;
    stats.totalLines += 1;

    let parsed: Record<string, unknown>;
    try {
      parsed = JSON.parse(line);
    } catch {
      stats.malformed += 1;
      continue;
    }

    const type = parsed.type;
    if (typeof type !== "string" || !BRIDGE_TYPES.has(type)) {
      stats.skippedNonBridge += 1;
      continue;
    }
    const id = parsed.id;
    if (typeof id !== "string" || !id) {
      stats.malformed += 1;
      continue;
    }
    const timestamp = typeof parsed.timestamp === "string" ? parsed.timestamp : new Date().toISOString();
    const text = typeof parsed.text === "string" ? parsed.text : "";

    if (opts.dryRun) {
      stats.appended += 1;
      continue;
    }

    const entry: Omit<WorkerEntry, "seq"> = {
      id,
      type: type as BridgeWorkerEntryType,
      text,
      timestamp,
      toolCallId: typeof parsed.toolCallId === "string" ? parsed.toolCallId : undefined,
      toolKind: typeof parsed.toolKind === "string" ? parsed.toolKind : undefined,
      status: typeof parsed.status === "string" ? parsed.status : undefined,
      raw: parsed.raw,
    };

    try {
      // appendWorkerEntry dedups by entry.id; replaying is safe.
      // We can't observe `appended` from this entrypoint, so we treat
      // any non-throwing call as success and post-tally with a count
      // delta below. For simplicity here we just count attempts; a
      // re-run reports the new dedup hits as `skippedDuplicate=0`
      // attempts because dedup happens server-side and is silent.
      await appendWorkerEntry(runId, workerId, entry);
      stats.appended += 1;
    } catch (error) {
      stats.malformed += 1;
      if (opts.verbose) {
        console.warn(`[backfill] ${workerId} line ${stats.totalLines} failed:`, error);
      }
    }
  }

  return stats;
}

The mapping isn't 1:1, so I need to align entries by ID and find where the tail entries start in the archive to understand what's actually missing from the head.

The key test is whether the filtered archive entries before the tail point equal exactly 1398—if so, reconstruction is straightforward. I should also check for any .idx files alongside the artifact_streams and consider stopping the watchdog during repair to avoid race conditions. Let me start with the alignment analysis.

/**
 * Compaction sweep for non-worker artifact streams.
 *
 * Run-level streams (execution_events / supervisor_interventions /
 * planning_review_findings) gzip to `<stream>.jsonl.gz` once the
 * owning run is in a terminal state AND the file hasn't been touched
 * for `minAgeMs`. The shared bytes layer in `append-only-store.ts`
 * already handles the chain+lock and atomic rename — this module just
 * picks candidates and calls into it.
 *
 * Worker streams keep their own sweep in `output-store.ts` until the
 * worker output-store relocation lands; the two will share this code
 * after that.
 */
import { promises as fs } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { inArray } from "drizzle-orm";
import { db } from "@/server/db";
import { artifactStreams, runs } from "@/server/db/schema";
import {
  compactArtifactStream,
  resolveArtifactStreamLocation,
} from "./append-only-store";
import { recordStreamCompaction } from "./stream-metadata";
import { resolveArtifactRoot } from "./project-root";
import {
  normalizeArtifactOwnerId,
  type ArtifactStreamKind,
} from "./stream-types";
import { isTerminalRunStatus } from "@/lib/run-status";
import { emitNamedEvent } from "@/server/events/named-events";

const DEFAULT_MIN_AGE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;

export async function compactStaleArtifactStreams(options: {
  minAgeMs?: number;
  now?: number;
  kinds?: ArtifactStreamKind[];
} = {}): Promise<{
  compacted: Array<{ runId: string; kind: ArtifactStreamKind; ownerId: string }>;
  errors: Array<{ runId: string; kind: ArtifactStreamKind; error: string }>;
}> {
  const minAgeMs = options.minAgeMs ?? DEFAULT_MIN_AGE_MS;
  const now = options.now ?? Date.now();
  const kinds: ArtifactStreamKind[] = options.kinds ?? [
    "execution_events",
    "supervisor_interventions",
    "planning_review_findings",
  ];

  const candidates = await db
    .select()
    .from(artifactStreams)
    .where(inArray(artifactStreams.kind, kinds));
  if (candidates.length === 0) return { compacted: [], errors: [] };

  const runIds: string[] = Array.from(new Set(candidates.map((c) => c.runId)));
  if (runIds.length === 0) return { compacted: [], errors: [] };
  const runRows = await db
    .select({ id: runs.id, status: runs.status, projectPath: runs.projectPath })
    .from(runs)
    .where(inArray(runs.id, runIds));
  type RunRow = { id: string; status: string; projectPath: string | null };
  const runById = new Map<string, RunRow>(runRows.map((r) => [r.id, r as RunRow] as const));

  const compacted: Array<{ runId: string; kind: ArtifactStreamKind; ownerId: string }> = [];
  const errors: Array<{ runId: string; kind: ArtifactStreamKind; error: string }> = [];

  for (const row of candidates) {
    const run = runById.get(row.runId);
    if (!run) continue;
    if (!isTerminalRunStatus(run.status)) continue;
    try {
      // Stat the plaintext to make sure it exists and is old enough.
      const root = await resolveArtifactRoot({ runId: row.runId, projectPath: run.projectPath ?? null }, "read");
      const filePath = path.join(root.absolutePath, row.relativePath);
      let stat;
      try {
        stat = await fs.stat(filePath);
      } catch (error) {
        if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") continue;
        throw error;
      }
      if (now - stat.mtimeMs < minAgeMs) continue;

      const location = await resolveArtifactStreamLocation(
        {
          runId: row.runId,
          kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
          projectPath: run.projectPath ?? null,
        },
        "read",
      );
      const ok = await compactArtifactStream(location);
      await recordStreamCompaction(
        {
          runId: row.runId,
          kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
        },
        ok,
        ok ? undefined : "compactArtifactStream returned false",
      );
      if (ok) {
        compacted.push({
          runId: row.runId,
          kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
          ownerId: normalizeArtifactOwnerId(row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId),
        });
        emitNamedEvent({
          kind: "artifact.compaction_completed",
          runId: row.runId,
          streamKind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
        });
      } else {
        emitNamedEvent({
          kind: "artifact.compaction_failed",
          runId: row.runId,
          streamKind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
          reason: "compactArtifactStream returned false",
        });
      }
    } catch (error) {
      const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
      errors.push({ runId: row.runId, kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind, error: message });
      await recordStreamCompaction(
        {
          runId: row.runId,
          kind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
          ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
        },
        false,
        message,
      );
      emitNamedEvent({
        kind: "artifact.compaction_failed",
        runId: row.runId,
        streamKind: row.kind as ArtifactStreamKind,
        ownerId: row.ownerId === "__none__" ? null : row.ownerId,
        reason: message,
      });
    }
  }
  return { compacted, errors };
}
